SEX ATTACKS Cops hunt man over three sexual assaults on different trains as CCTV released

COPS have release CCTV in the urgent hunt for a man following a string of alleged sexual assaults on different trains.

The victims were all reportedly targeted on services travelling from London to Essex over a five-month period.



British Transport Police said: “Detectives investigating three sexual assaults on board trains to Essex have released these images in connection.

“Shortly after midnight on 5 July, a man sexually assaulted a woman while travelling on a service from London to Benfleet.



“The same man is believed to have committed a sexual assault and an attempted sexual assault in March 2026, again on services between London and Essex.

“In one incident, the man left the train at Westcliff-on-Sea.

“Detectives believe the man in the images could have information that may assist their enquiries.

“Anyone who recognises him is asked to text BTP on 61016, or call 0800 40 50 40, using the reference Op Valhalla.

“Information can also be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Will it rain this weekend? Latest Met Office weather forecast for the August bank holiday in the UK
News.content:
BRITS gearing up for the August bank holiday are keeping a close eye on the skies.

After a relatively sunny and settled start, the final week of meteorological summer is expected to bring a shift in the weather.



Experts predict a wave of low pressure to sweep in from the south.

So if you’re planning a weekend BBQ or a staycation, you may need to keep the umbrellas on standby alongside the sun cream.



Will it rain this bank holiday weekend?

At the time of writing, it’s looking like a mixed bag for the extended weekend.

The Met Office says an area of low pressure is forecast to sweep in from the Atlantic just as the bank holiday begins.



That will bring with it unsettled conditions, though where you are in the country could prove key.

The service says north-western areas currently appear the most likely to experience the driest conditions over the three-day break.

Heading into Friday, both Northern Ireland and western Scotland will enjoy some of the best conditions, with plenty of sunshine and comfortable temperatures in the high teens to low twenties.

For the rest of the UK, conditions will be far more hit-and-miss as damp, muggy weather takes over.



Forecasters say there could be a “brief respite from the unsettled conditions early on Saturday”, giving you a potential window to fire up the grill, hit the beach, or get out for a walk.

Don’t get too comfortable though – further spells of rain and showers are likely to develop as the weekend progresses into Sunday and Bank Holiday Monday.

What is the weather doing this week?

The shift in weather will be felt well before Saturday arrives.

The Met Office says the UK is facing a “marked change in the weather” as the week progresses.

While Tuesday, August 25 offered a pleasant day for many, Wednesday will see the risk of showers and thunderstorms increase across the south and west.



That forecast has prompted a yellow weather warning across a large chunk of England and Wales.

Despite the looming storms, temperatures will remain high, reaching the mid-to-high twenties.

Thursday is currently tipped to be the hottest day of the week, with temperatures hitting 28C in parts of southern and eastern England.

But a yellow warning for thunderstorms remains in place from 6am to 10pm.

The Met Office says there will be “increasing humidity, warmer temperatures and a growing risk of heavy rain and thunderstorms.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Some areas could see 30 to 40mm of rainfall in a very short space of time, bringing a risk of surface water flooding, hail and lightning.

By Friday, the forecast becomes even more unpredictable as the low-pressure system shifts north-eastwards, taking the heaviest rain towards northern and eastern parts of England.

News.title: Raging bulls kill 2 & injure 11 as spectators are hurled in air & thrown like rag dolls by beasts set loose in streets
News.content:
RAGING bulls have killed two people and injured 11, hurling spectators in the air like rag dolls as they charge through the streets at a festival.

Juan Manuel Filomeno Herrera, 29, died from serious head and chest injuries after he was gored at a gory Mexican version of Pamplona’s famous Running of the Bulls festival.



Luis Xolocotzi Ramirez, 57, suffered a skull fracture and gore injury to his chest at Saturday’s event in Huamantla, east of Mexico City.

He had to be rushed to hospital by air ambulance, where he died of his injuries.





A 24-year-old American woman from Texas is reportedly among those hospitalised at this year’s Huamantlada festival.

It saw 21 fighting bulls let loose in the street.

Injuries included a woman who was thrown in the air by one of the huge animals and struck in the face.

Terrifying footage shows her attempting to flee the animal as it charged at her.



But it catches the woman with its horns and flips her over its back.

She crashes to the ground in front of horrified onlookers, as the bull rounds on her again.

The woman is knocked over once more, but scrambles to her feet and runs for her life before being helped to safety.



More harrowing video shows one of the men thought to have lost his life at the festival being charged at and gored.

The clip shows him being tossed in the air before his is dragged away.

The deaths were the first for eight years at the festival.

Juan, the youngest fatality, lived locally.

He is said to have been gored by a bull after losing his balance and falling to the ground.



Many people questioned the festival’s traditions after the deaths.

Bruno Gonzalez shared a photo of Juan and wrote on Facebook: “At what point does tradition become thoughtlessness, violence and negligence?

“And when it becomes that, is it worth perpetuating it over time? May he rest in peace.”

It comes after several people were injured at this year’s running of the bulls at Pamplona’s San Fermín festival.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They included a Brit tourist who was rushed to hospital.



William Mitchinson, 24, was trampled as he tried to outrun the animals on the half-mile course in the north of Spain.

News.title: Simple recalls MORE ‘contaminated’ make-up remover products over ‘microbiological risk’ that can damage eyes
News.content:
SIMPLE has recalled more “contaminated” make-up remover products which have been identified as a “microbiological risk” that can cause “eye inflammation”.

The notice now includes 16 affected batches of the product.



Skincare giant Simple has expanded a prior recall notice for its Kind to Skin Micellar Cleansing Water over affected batches that may be microbiologically contaminated.

The recall notice originally applied to two batches of the 730ml Micellar Water.



It has now expanded to include more batch codes of the 730ml Micellar Water and a number of 200ml and 400ml bottles too.

A total of 16 batches have now been recalled.



Full list of products included in the recall: Simple Kind to Skin Micellar Cleansing Water 200ml – 610041, 611641, 615941

– 610041, 611641, 615941 Simple Kind to Skin Micellar Cleansing Water 400ml – 611141, 611341, 611441, 613341, 613441, 614541, 614741, 614841

– 611141, 611341, 611441, 613341, 613441, 614541, 614741, 614841 Simple Kind to Skin Micellar Cleansing Water 730ml – 613841, 613941, 611041, 616641, 616741

Sold in discount retailers B&M, Home Bargains, and Savers, the affected batches “may be microbiologically contaminated”.

According to the company website, the specific batch codes are being recalled due to the “possible presence of bacteria”, which could cause “eye inflammation” for consumers.

As a result, the products do not meet the requirements of Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 (the ‘Cosmetics Regulation’).

The batch code number can be found on the bottom of the make-up remover bottle.



The skincare company has said that no other Simple products have been affected by this issue.

Customers have been urged to stop using the product immediately and to contact the UK customer careline for Unilever, which is listed on the Simple website.

No proof of purchase is required when applying for a refund, with Simple only requesting a photograph of the product showing the affected batch code.

Simple has advised any consumers with concerns about their health to seek advice from a medical professional.

A statement from Simple on the product recall page said: “We understand that product recalls can be concerning, and we are sorry for any concern or inconvenience this may have caused.”

News.title: Country to pay parents £40,000 per child in desperate measure to boost plummeting birth rate
News.content:
CASH FOR BUMPS Country to pay parents £40,000 per child in desperate measure to boost plummeting birth rate

SINGAPORE is offering to pay parents a whopping £40,000 per child in a desperate bid to boost the country’s plummeting birth rates.

The major measure has been announced by the government to try and persuade young people to start a family after Singapore registered a record-low fertility rate last year.



Lawrence Wong, the city- state’s prime minister, said the total funding would be around 70,000 Singaporean dollars or £40,000.

The payment would not be a one-time deal at birth but rather paid in installments up until the child reaches the age of 17.



An initial reward of S$10,000 (£7,300) would be handed out as a “baby gift” with a similarly valued incentive awarded for completing higher education at the age of 17.

Education, health and child support grants would also be available to new parents as well as reduced nursery care fees for pre-school children.



Childcare leave will be increased with its cost fully covered by the government, rather than employers.

Companies currently have to pay for childcare with the money only partially reimbursed.

Families applying for government-subsidised flats will also have an increased chance of winning allocation ballots for each additional child.

Wong hopes it will mark “a fundamental shift in how we support families”.



How China will crumble as world superpower with population to crash by BILLION in decades CHINA’S superpower status could soon crumble – with its population on track to plummet by over a billion in the coming decades. XI Jinping‘s regime is set to be exposed on the world stage as years of deceit, inflated numbers and worrying demographic shifts finally take their toll, experts warn. Worrying statistics show that the population could drop from 1.4billion to 390 million in less than 75 year if China’s birth rates continue to plunge as death rates surge at their current rate. As of early 2026, China claims to have over 1.4 billion residents, per official national records. But Yi Fuxian, a leading critic of China‘s one-child policy, and many demographers believe this figure is on track to rapidly drop due to the high number of elderly Chinese citizens and falling birth rates. As of 2026, the median age in China is around 40-years-old with an estimated 15 per cent of citizens being over 65-years-old. These figures are around the average for a major world economy. But below the surface, the figures are a cause for concern. China recorded a historic low in births in 2024, sitting at only 7.92 million – the lowest since 1939. Back then the population sat at just over 500 million. China also has one of the lowest fertility rates in the world, at around just one birth per woman – far below the average replacement rate of 2.1 per woman. Declining births is a trend which has worsened dramatically over time in China – with little sign of improving in the near future. In a chilling prediction, Yi says: “Assuming China is lucky enough to stabilise its fertility rate at 1.0, its population will fall to 1.06 billion in 2050 and 390 million in 2100.” Read more here.

He said: “Today, families everywhere are under growing pressure.

“We want every family to know: if you choose to have children, the government will stand with you.

“We will provide more support, and over more years.”

Worrying statistics show that Singapore, along with several other Asian countries, are facing a demographic crisis.



A survey of nearly 500 Singaporean adults aged 18-44 found that almost a quarter have no plans to have children, according to a YouGov poll.

In the same survey, 30 per cent said there was nothing the government could do to make them want children.

Singapore, with a population of just over six million, registered a fertility rate of 0.87 children per woman last year.

This was down from 0.97 in 2024 and closing in on South Korea’s world-lowest rate of 0.8.

Experts believe a fertility rate of 2.1 is required to maintain a stable population.



Another major issue is Singapore’s ageing population.

One in four Singaporeans are expected to be aged over 65 by 2030.

This would categorise them as “super-aged” by the United Nations.

An older civilisation paired with young adults not wanting children could have dire consequences.

Wong continued: “Despite all that we do to support families, we have to be realistic.



“Our total fertility rate is still likely to fall far short of replacement.

“If we relied only on births, our citizen population will shrink. We would age more rapidly.

“And there would be fewer younger Singaporeans to support a growing number of seniors.”

News.title: At least 8 dead including two children after gunman opens fire at home before setting it on fire and killing himself
News.content:
AT LEAST eight members of the same family have died after a gunman opened fire on their Montana home.

Several family members were left trapped inside of the home after the suspect set it on fire, letting it burn to the ground.



A 911 call came in reporting an active shooting at the home in Billings, Montana just after 6pm on Monday, where gunfire could be heard on the call, according to Yellowstone County Sheriff Kent O’Donnell.

Police arrived roughly ten minutes after the 911 came in and found a man in the backyard while gunfire could still be heard and the house was seen surrounded by smoke, according to the Billings Gazette.



The man was transported to a local hospital at 6:48pm — where he later died — after police found him with a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

The incident began as a family disturbance, but the gunman’s relation to the victims was not immediately clear.

All of the victims were identified by police, but names were not immediately released except for two children identified through a GoFundMe set up for the family.

One fundraiser was set up for Adam Ghekiere, an airport rescue firefighter, whose wife, children and other members of his family were killed.



Two of the victims were identified as 15-year-old Landon and 12-year-old Charlotte in another GoFundMe.

Ghekiere and Erica Jarussi Schneider are the parents of the two children and were not at the home at the time of the incident, the Daily Mail reported.

The children’s stepfather Danny was also not at the scene, per the outlet.

Landon was preparing to start his sophomore year of high school while Charlotte was entering the seventh grade, according to the GoFundMe.

Landon was described as “a loving, caring young man who was always willing to lend a hand to his family and neighbors.



“He was looking forward to getting his driver’s license this week and was a patient, protective, and loving big brother.”

“Funny, precocious, and adorable — with just the right amount of stubborn— Charlotte had an angelic smile and loved posing for pictures,” the fundraiser read.

Officials say it could take days to determine what led up to the shooting, adding it would be “reckless” to send investigators into the house where they could damage evidence.

The house became fully engulfed in flames soon after authorities arrived, posing challenges for first responders as there was no fire hydrant in the subdivision.

The origin of the fire was not immediately clear, and the investigation remains ongoing, officials said.



“When the fire was observed in the structure, fire suppression efforts took priority as the fire blocked any reasonable attempt to rescue or recover victims,” Billings Police Department Assistant Chief Shawn Mayo said at a press conference.

Authorities had to coordinate closely when responding to the scene to balance the safety of responders with the need for fire prevention.

“Because the scene could not be immediately confirmed as secured, our firefighters were unable to operate as we normally would,” Billings Fire Department Chief Matt Hoppel said.

“The delay and limited access presented significant challenges.

“Fire conditions continued to worsen, and the residence ultimately became heavily involved and was consumed by fire.”



“You could hear a couple gunshots going off and then I looked out front and the house was on fire, about three houses down,” neighbor Dave Hiller told KTVQ.

“There was smoke just pluming from the house.

“This was a house where you saw a family out front all the time,” he told KTVQ.

News.title: I was guinea pig for ‘Britain’s most evil’ mum who performed depraved acts on my little brother…I still hear his screams
News.content:
WATCHING her gravely ill little brother Matthew scream in pain while their mother Lisa Hayden-Johnson inserted a feeding tube into him as a child is a memory that still haunts Laura, now 27, to this day.

Lisa was known as a doting mum to Matthew, who’d been dubbed “Britain’s Sickest Child”, but it later turned out to all be a lie fabricated by the sick mum – and chillingly Laura later realised she’d also been used as a “test subject”.



Lisa said Matthew was allergic to almost every food, had to be fed through a tube and needed an oxygen tank, wheelchair and a cocktail of drugs for illnesses including diabetes, cerebral palsy and cystic fibrosis.

In the Channel 4 documentary, Love You To Death, Laura, Matthew and Lisa herself give their accounts of how Lisa went from being seen as a selfless, loving parent to being dubbed “Britain’s most evil mother,” as it was revealed the only person making Matthew sick was herself.

Now, in an exclusive interview with The Sun, Laura tells us how, as the older sibling, her childhood was ripped apart and how the full extent of what her mother did to them both, gives her nightmares.



She says: “It was only recently I realised that her behaviour before Matthew was born was weird.

“I must have been in Year Four at primary school when a friend told me there was a picture of me inside the doors of the arts and crafts cupboard.

“I had a look and there was a note from my mum to the teacher saying that if I was staring into the distance, they needed to contact an ambulance.

“I kind of accepted it until a couple of years ago when I downloaded the NHS app and I got my medical records and read reports where my mum was claiming I was having fits and seizures, saying I was in and out of hospital.

“But I have no memory of that at all. I was on seizure medication until the age of six or seven.



“I was like a test subject for my mum. It had happened to me first, before she switched to Matthew.”

Laura, now 27, remembers the early years of her childhood, growing up in a seaside house in Brixham, Devon with her cherubic baby brother and mum and dad, Lisa and Chris, fondly.

When she was born, her mother called her “Princess” because, recalls Laura Johnson, “She said I came out looking beautiful.”

A second child, Matthew, was born two years later in 2001.

“They were brilliant parents,” she tells us.



“My dad was absolutely besotted with my mum.

“He used to work on the banana counter at Morrisons, so mum did nearly all of the childcare.”

But those good memories are cruelly short for Laura, who quickly found herself in a new role of helping her mum, Lisa, care around the clock for her little brother, who was born prematurely and needed constant attention.



After a police investigation exposed her years of lying, Lisa Hayden-Johnson was given a 39-month sentence for child cruelty and perverting the course of justice between 2001 and 2007.

She was diagnosed with the rare condition of Munchausen by Proxy (now known as Fabrication Induced Illness) – a form of abuse in which an individual, usually the mother, feigns, exaggerates or induces illness in her own child in order to gain attention and sympathy.

She was released in 2011, having served 19 months.

“I get told a lot by people to just move on,” Laura says.

“But it’s hard because my whole life was flipped upside down.”



At a time when she should have been enjoying the best years of her young life, she became carer not only for her brother but also her father – and then her mother.

Even as an adult she has learnt disturbing new truths, like the shocking realisation that she was a “test trial” for what happened to Matthew and learning from family members, that her mother’s claim that she had a twin who died in utero was false.

Despite it all, Laura remains level-headed and even holds a certain amount of sympathy for her mother, but admits that her feelings are “difficult and conflicting” switching between sympathy and anger.

But she holds the slimmest hope that, having heard their side of the story, her mum might finally apologise.

“I hope she will maybe start to appreciate the harm she did cause to me and Matthew, but I don’t think she’ll ever fully be able to process that and acknowledge that to the point where she apologises for it correctly,” she says.



“I don’t want a, ‘Sorry that happened, but that wasn’t my fault.’ I want a real apology, and, in my heart, I don’t think that will ever happen.

“The only way bridges could be made is if she went and got help and actually proved that.

“But it’s something that she’s been offered multiple times and she’s just in complete denial that she needs any help at all.”



Despite his shockingly abusive early years which saw him in and out of hospital and undergoing nine general anaesthetics and four invasive operations before he was six, Matthew feels like it was his sister who suffered the greatest.

“Because I was so young at the time, my memories are very fragmented and I think that’s played a part in how I’ve been able to move on a bit quicker than Laura,” he tells us.

“There’s not much pain I remember and I don’t have that feeling of having missed out on experiences because I don’t remember ever having the chance to have them in the first place.

“Making the documentary was helpful for me to gain information and has kind of helped me put it behind me further.

“I was concerned about my mum taking part in it, but I sort of knew that if she was asked, then she would want to take part in the narrative.



“But I was quite taken back by what she says in the documentary.

“She clearly has no remorse or understanding of what she’s done.

“With Laura being older, it impacted her more than it did me. I know she’s strong but I do believe she struggled with it.”

Laura admits she still has nightmares from her traumatic past.

She adds: “I have big memories of hospitals, doctors and nurses. These are things I still dream about now and have nightmares – seeing Matthew as this little boy who just looked so unwell.



“Every other day his feeding tube needed replacing.

What is Munchausen syndrome? MUNCHAUSEN syndrome is a psychological condition where someone pretends to be ill or deliberately produces symptoms of illness in themselves. People with Munchausen syndrome can behave in a number of different ways, including: Pretending to have psychological symptoms – for example, claiming to hear voices or claiming to see things that are not really there

Pretending to have physical symptoms – for example, claiming to have chest pain or a stomach ache

Actively trying to get ill – such as deliberately infecting a wound by rubbing dirt into it The condition is complex and poorly understood, though it’s thought it could be brought on by emotional trauma or personality disorders. Source: NHS

“I would be in bed when I would suddenly hear Matthew kicking up a fuss. He would be screaming, like he was being stabbed.

“I remember being petrified for him and feeling helpless because I couldn’t help him.

“Now, as an adult, I can still hear him screaming.”

After her mum went to prison and Laura and Matthew moved with their dad to Sheffield, Laura continued to feel the weight of responsibility on her young shoulders.



She says: “My dad struggled to get over what had happened and unlike Matthew, who was enjoying being a normal, healthy boy and making friends at school, I missed my old friends and was bullied at school.

“I felt like an outsider and my confidence went completely downhill.

“I think my dad struggled with that.

“He became quite closed off emotionally, I think probably to protect his own feelings, understandably so, but because of that, our relationship changed.

“I don’t think my dad really knew how to look after a young girl. I needed my mum.”



At their mother’s request, Laura and Matthew had started visiting her after her release from prison, with a social worker in attendance.

“Eventually, I had a massive breakdown at home and that’s when my mum said, ‘Well, why don’t you move in with me?’ I didn’t think anything bad could come from it.”

Laura was then 16 and at first enjoyed life with mum, going shopping with her and feeling like they were bonding.

“I was so focused on having a good time that my brain switched off about what she had done,” she says.

But then Lisa’s craving for drama and attention turned on herself as she complained of being unwell and needed Laura to push her around in a wheelchair.



Lisa would also regularly regress into a five-year old, watching Peppa Pig and self-harming herself.

“I was like a carer again,” says Laura.

When she decided she’d had enough and moved out, Lisa was suddenly well again.

“From a young age I’d had it drilled in to me to care for other people,” says Laura.

“That shifted from caring for Matthew to helping my dad through a difficult time to then moving in with my mum and caring for her.



“It was something that came natural to me that I felt I needed to do.

“I just wanted to look after her and protect her from herself, really.”

Laura had been let down once, as a young girl, when all the focus was on Matthew.



Now, having given her mother a second chance, she was sadly let down again.

She and Matthew cut all ties with their mother, who has since re-married and says she is “happy, living an amazing life, married to the most amazing guy”.

Laura, who lives with her partner of seven years and works in childcare and Matthew, who lives on his own and works in admin and enjoys a good circle of friends, remain on good terms with their father, who is now in a new relationship.

Chris has always refused to have anything to do with Lisa since her lies were exposed and did not take part in the documentary.

“I think he’s a bit concerned about the public attention being drawn back to it,” says Laura.



“He worries because he was naturally close to mum, as her husband, and that people might think he should have stopped what she was doing.

“But he wasn’t aware of it at all.

“I do think he’s somewhat supportive of us in processing it in the way we have with the documentary but he just wants to put it to rest and move on himself, as well.”

Laura and Matthew’s scarred childhood has cemented an unbreakable bond between them.

“It’s always been me and him against everybody and that’s what solidified our relationship,” she says.



“When mum went to prison, I was there for that caring role of looking after him, making sure he was okay mentally and also when he was feeling physically poorly.

“We will always have a strong bond because it’s not a normal kind of sibling relationship.

“It’s more that we’re both there to support each other because we know exactly what each other’s gone through. We can relate like that.”

“It definitely plays a big part,” adds Matthew. “We’ve always been close and still are.

“Having the support of someone who has been on that same journey is nice.



“It’s comforting to be able to deal with it together, rather than on our own.”

All three parts of Love You To Death are now available to stream on Channel 4.

News.title: ‘Joyriders’ killed with two cops in wrong-way smash were ‘chasing down rivals in revenge for gang attack before horror’
News.content:
THE stolen car involved in a fatal wrong-way collision that killed seven people had been pursuing a rival gang as part of a violent feud, it is claimed.

In the early hours of Saturday a VW Passat ploughed into a patrol car, claiming the lives of PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.



Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18, were all also killed in the tragic collision.

Twelve people were arrested in connection with the tragedy yesterday, with five more, including a 16-year-old boy, arrested by detectives investigating the events leading up to the crash today.



It has since been revealed that the VW Passat that the five young men were in had been chasing a rival gang who used a Volvo XC60 to ram into the home of Cole Worthy’s dad just 40 minutes before the fatal collision.

The Daily Mail reports that a home belonging to Gye Worthy was rammed twice by the Volvo, which reversed into the front window, causing extensive damage.

Minutes later the Passat was racing through Middlesbrough with Worthy and four of his friends inside.

They were allegedly pursuing the Volvo involved in the attack on Worthy’s dad’s home.



It was while the Passat was speeding through the town that a police patrol spotted it, and a chase ensued.

Police pursued the Volkswagen Passat in the early hours of Saturday morning after the plates activated an ANPR camera, the Independent Office for Police Conduct said.

Officers then chased the car through Middlesbrough for just under seven minutes before the cops called off the pursuit when the Passat joined the A66.

Just 10 seconds later, at 3.39am, the car ploughed into another marked armed-response vehicle carrying two officers.

The vehicle was travelling on the correct side of the carriageway and had not been part of the high-speed chase but was in the area to assist.



Initial reports suggested the five young men were “TikTok joyriders” after it was revealed that Makai previously posted several videos to TikTok which appear to show him in a high-speed police chase.

Saddington had also shared clips to social media showing him driving dangerously.

However, the Daily Mail reports that the five young men were in fact part of an organised criminal network operating across Teesside.



There is no suggestion that Cole Worthy’s dad, Gye Worthy, 39, was involved in any criminal activity, but the attack on his home is believed to have sparked the chase.

A neighbour said: “The huge bang woke everyone up and it was then followed by a second.

“Whatever happened was quick because, by the time my husband looked out of the window, the car was gone, but there was very bad damage to the house.”



And a source claimed: “After the attack on his father’s house, Cole Worthy and his mates were out in the VW Passat looking for whoever had done this. When they fight among themselves it is one thing, but when innocent lives like those of two police officers are lost, that’s completely another.”

According to Cleveland Police, both the Volvo and the Passat were part of their enquiries in the aftermath of the tragic wrong-way smash.

It is understood that the Volvo rammed Worthy’s home at around 3am, by 3.36am, the Passat was in a high- speed police chase which was called off seconds before the devastating crash when the vehicle went the wrong way down the A66.

Four of the five young men killed in the horror A66 smash had previous convictions.

Previous convictions of four occupants Cole Worthy Use threatening abusive language to cause harassment, alarm and distress on 27 October 2024 and pleaded guilty Failing to surrender to custody on 14 May 2025 and pleaded guilty Common assault of a police officer on 27 April 2025 and pleaded guilty Driving without a licence on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Using a vehicle without insurance on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving without reasonable consideration on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving using a mobile phone on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Jakub Matusiak Using a vehicle without insurance on 22 March 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving without a licence on 22 March 2026 and pleaded guilty Makai Saddington Possession of a controlled class C drug on 31 May 2025 and pleaded guilty Possession of a knife in a public place on 31 May 2025 and pleaded guilty 11 October 2025 three offences for assaulting a police officer and pleaded guilty Assaulted a police officer on 9 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Racially aggravated intentional harassment, alarm and distress on 9 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Theo Rae 12 shoplifting offences between 21 October 2023 and 4 May 2024 and pleaded guilty to all offences Three thefts from motor vehicle offences between 31 January 2024 and 25 September 2024 and pleaded guilty to all offences One theft of vehicle on 13 April 2024 and pleaded guilty Possession of cannabis on 22 April 2024 and pleaded guilty Aggravated vehicle taking on 16 May 2024 and pleaded guilty Aggravated vehicle taking 2 January 2025 and pleaded guilty Conviction of an offence while a youth rehabilitation order is in force on 26 February 2025 and pleaded guilty Assaulted a police officer on 30 April 2026 and pleaded guilty Michael Robert Cahill No convictions

Saddington pleaded guilty to possession of a Class C drug and a knife in May 2025, and months later admitted three offences of assaulting a police officer.



Meanwhile, Worthy admitted using threatening and abusive language to cause harassment, alarm and distress in October 2024.

In March, Matusiak admitted using a vehicle without insurance and driving without a licence.

And Rae was convicted of assaulting a police officer, shoplifting, stealing cars, theft, drug possession and breaching a youth rehabilitation order.

As police continue to probe the tragic collision, 12 people were arrested in connection with the incident yesterday with five more taken into custody today.

The alleged offences include possession of a firearm and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.



Some of those arrested over the A66 investigation are suspected of “participating in the activities of an organised crime group” Cleveland Police confirmed.

The force said: “On the morning of Saturday 22 August, Cleveland Police received several reports of two vehicles being driven dangerously.

“The first vehicle, which is believed to be a Volvo XC60, was witnessed ramming properties in the Middlesbrough area.



“The second vehicle, a Volkswagen Passat, is believed to have been associated with the activities of the Volvo XC60.

“Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates to avoid detection but were picked up by the force’s automated number plate recognition technology.

“The Volvo XC60 involved in the initial reports has been traced and recovered in Middlesbrough as part of the criminal investigation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Throughout the course of the weekend, Cleveland Police, supported by officers and staff from Durham, Northumbria and North Yorkshire Police, have worked tirelessly to establish the circumstances that led to the fatal collision.

“Those enquiries have resulted in the arrests of 12 people across Teesside.”

News.title: EasyJet's hiring 100s of new flight attendants - but you must meet 9 criteria
News.content:
EasyJet's hiring 100s of new flight attendants - but you must meet 9 criteria

EasyJet is about to launch its latest recruitment drive and is looking to hire hundreds of new flight attendants

View 2 Images EasyJet is encouraging older people to apply (Image: David Parry/PA Media Assignments)

EasyJet is about to hire hundreds of new flight attendants - but you have to meet certain requirements to join.

‌



The budget airline recruitment drive begins next month. This year, easyJet has particularly encouraged older people to apply. Since first launching its initiative to recruit older workers in 2022, the number of cabin crew over the age of 50 more than doubled at the airline, with the number of over-60s almost quadrupling in numbers.

‌



However, you don't have to be in the OAP camp to apply. You don't even need aviation experience. But you will need to:

‌



View 2 Images The application period opens next month (Image: David Parry/PA Media Assignments)

Be 18 years or older

Be between 5’2” (157.5 cm) and 6’3” (190 cm) without shoes

Be fluent in written and spoken English as well as the language native to your base

Hold a valid passport with unrestricted travel across the UK, EEA, and the easyJet network. (Skilled Worker visa sponsorship is not available)

Live within 90 minutes of your chosen base or willing to relocate

Have no visible tattoos on the head, face, or neck (all tattoos must be inoffensive)

Be comfortable selling items from our CAFE.SHOP range, including alcohol (this contributes to commission earnings)

Be able to swim 25 metres unaided, tread water, inflate a life jacket, and climb in and out of a life raft

Pass a UK CAA or EASA Cabin Crew medical and fit securely into a jump seat

EasyJet is particularly keen to have applications from people who:

‌



Have at least 6 months’ experience in a customer-facing or people-focused role

Communicate clearly, confidently, and kindly

Stay calm under pressure and make safe, well-informed decisions

Enjoy working as part of a diverse, energetic team

Take ownership, solve problems with empathy, and go the extra mile for customers

EasyJet began its 'Returnships’ initiative in 2024, offering free in-person and online cabin crew taster sessions for hundreds of interested career changers over 50. Francesca Hicks was part of the process.

Aged 64 and a former secretary and nurse for those living with dementia, Francesca was seeking an opportunity to adapt her skills and broaden her horizons. She attended a taster open day, submitted her formal application, and completed a series of interviews before joining her easyJet cabin crew training course. A year and a half on, she is now a fully trained cabin crew member and has taken to the skies over 250 times.

‌



Francesca Hicks said: “When the opportunity to join easyJet as cabin crew came up, I jumped at the chance. I knew I already held all the skills required for the job, but it gave me another way to use my communication, organisation and interpersonal skills in a new and exciting setting.

“The reception both I and my fellow new joiners have received has been overwhelmingly positive. This, and the experiences I’ve had over the past 18 months, have given me a confidence and sense of fulfilment that I’ll take with me through the next stage of my career.”

Michael Brown, director of cabin services at easyJet, said: “It’s been incredibly encouraging to see the numbers of cabin crew over 50 more than double since 2022 - evidence that many are increasingly viewing cabin crew as a fantastic career pivot regardless of age.

Article continues below

“We want more over 50s to apply as they not only bring their existing skills to excel in a career at easyJet, but also a wealth of life experience that is appreciated by our customers and colleagues alike, which is at the heart of the fantastic service our crew is known for.

“With hundreds of cabin crew roles set to be available across the UK, we would encourage even more to apply, and we look forward to seeing this community at easyJet grow further in the years to come.”

To find out more about being cabin crew at easyJet, visit easyJet Cabin Crew.

News.title: UK weather maps show thunderstorms hitting 16 counties in just two hours – list
News.content:
UK weather maps show thunderstorms hitting 16 counties in just two hours – list

Heavy rain and lightning are coming this week, with the Met Office having already issued two weather warnings, and several areas could see thunderstorms across a wild two-hour period

View 3 Images Map shows where thunderstorms are likely at 2pm on Wednesday (Image: Ventusky)

Thunderstorms are expected in the UK this week, with weather models showing at least 16 counties facing heavy rain and lightning across just two hours on Wednesday.

‌



BBC Weather says thundery showers are expected in southern parts of England and Wales tonight, before progressing slowly northwards tomorrow. Some showers are expected in Northern Ireland and southern Scotland by the afternoon and evening, the BBC adds.

‌



Further rain and thunderstorms should follow on Thursday, according to BBC Weather, with northern areas most at risk then.

‌



Weather modelling data suggests the south and south-east will see the worst of the thunderstorms at around 2pm on Wednesday, with London potentially in line for heavy rain.

View 3 Images Map shows where thunderstorms are likely at 4pm on Wednesday (Image: Ventusky)

UK weather maps show 13 counties face heavy rain on Thursday with thunderstorms READ MORE :

Just two hours later at 4pm on Wednesday, the models show potential thunderstorms stretching as far north as Staffordshire. In total, the data suggests 16 counties could see serious thunderstorms across those two hours.

‌



UK counties facing thunderstorms on Wednesday

Sussex

Surrey

Kent

Middlesex

Hampshire

Wiltshire

Buckinghamshire

Berkshire

Essex

Bedfordshire

Northamptonshire

Warwickshire

Leicestershire

Derbyshire

Staffordshire

Nottinghamshire

Met Office weather forecast

The Met Office forecast is very similar to BBC Weather, and predicts “heavy showers and thunderstorms” will develop tonight - and could potentially reach Northern Ireland before Wednesday.

The Met Office adds for Wednesday: “Bands of heavy showers and thunderstorms will continue to move northwards through the day. Sunnier moments in between, where it will feel very warm and humid, especially in the south.”

‌



View 3 Images Areas covered by Met Office weather warning on Wednesday (Image: Met Office)

The Met Office has issued a weather warning for thunderstorms on Wednesday, spanning 59 areas across England and Wales. It is in place from 3am and lasts until 10pm. A second warned has been issued for Thursday.

‘Spanish plume’ causing thunderstorms

BBC Weather said a “Spanish plume type of system” could be responsible for the thunderstorms this week.

Article continues below

‘Spanish plume’ is a meteorological term referring to warm air moving northward from Spain which rises and cools, leading to the formation of thunder clouds in the UK

The Met Office explains: “As cooler air spreads from the west, instability increases and the very warm air rises through the cooler air, enhancing the formation of thunderstorms.”

Despite this, temperatures are expected to remain above average this week - potentially peaking at 28C in southern areas on Wednesday.

News.title: Expert warns Brits 'overwhelmed' by money jargon are avoiding their finances
News.content:
Expert warns Brits 'overwhelmed' by money jargon are avoiding their finances

Personal finance expert Rajan Lakhani warns that not understanding key phrases like 'capital gains' and 'compound interest' could cost people dearly, and urges banks to offer clearer explanations.

View 3 Images Money jargon means some Brits are avoiding their finances altogether (Image: Getty Images)

The 25 most baffling financial terms and acronyms include 'capital gains', 'compound interest' and 'variable rate'. A survey of 2,000 adults found that 56% feel overwhelmed by financial jargon, with 42% admitting it puts them off investing altogether.

‌



Almost a third (31%) don't fully grasp what 'capital gains' means, while 23% aren't confident they could explain what 'APR' stands for. Others struggle to understand what an 'unarranged overdraft' (17%), 'credit score' (17%) or 'standing order' (15%) actually means.

‌



The research also revealed that fewer than one in five (17%) feel they completely understand the upcoming changes to ISAs, which will see the Cash ISA allowance changed from £20,000 a year to £12,000 for under 65s, as well as a 22% tax on interest earned on uninvested cash held within a Stocks & Shares ISA.

‌



Even amongst those who claimed at least some understanding of the changes, 41% could not correctly identify the new Cash ISA allowance as £12,000.

View 3 Images Misunderstanding financial jargon can affect Brits’ money decisions (Image: Getty Images)

The study was commissioned by smart money app Plum, which is helping to demystify the confusion by creating a glossary of the most perplexing financial terms.

‌



Rajan Lakhani, personal finance expert for the app said: "Finances can be tricky to navigate, especially with the forthcoming changes to Cash ISAs and Stocks & Shares ISAs.

"Money is something we deal with every day and not understanding something related to our personal finances could cost us dearly. But some of the jargon can be overwhelming – leaving many people simply avoiding their finances and possibly missing out as a result."

He added: "For example, investing has historically been the most reliable way to help avoid inflation eroding the value of your money in the long-term, yet many people are missing out because they don't understand the terms.

‌



"We want people to feel confident managing their money, so hope these clear explanations of the most confusing terms will help when someone isn't sure what something means and how it will impact them."

View 3 Images Low confidence is stopping many Brits from investing (Image: Getty Images)

The research revealed that 28% of adults have no confidence in understanding information from banks and financial providers, with 54% feeling overwhelmed when it comes to making savings and investment decisions.

‌



The internet remains the go-to resource for financial decision-making (41%), ahead of banks (29%) and family members (21%). However, 27% of Gen Z turn to social media for guidance, compared to just 1% of Boomers.

Clearer explanations from banks (51%), financial education in schools (46%) and the use of less jargon in emails and correspondence (43%) were all cited as key solutions to improving understanding.

Rajan Lakhani, from Plum, added: "The research shows confusion about financial terminology makes decisions about money more daunting. It also highlights that many people are not turning to reliable, curated and regulated sources of information.

Article continues below

"We hope by making bitesize financial information accessible and easier to understand, we can help people of all generations feel assured taking control of their finances and planning for the future."

News.title: Mum attacked by shark said its face was 'horrific' and she only survived by thinking of her daughter
News.content:
Mum attacked by shark said its face was 'horrific' and she only survived by thinking of her daughter

'She's not going to have a mum' - thought Leah Stewart about her daughter as she was being attacked by great white shark which she desperately fought off

View 4 Images Leah Stewart said thoughts of her daughter helped her survive shark attack (Image: Jam Press/GoFundMe)

A woman who lost part of her arm in a shark attack in Australia has said the thought of her 18-month-old daughter helped her to survive.

‌



In her first public remarks since the attack two months ago off the coast of Sydney Leah Stewart, 35, said: "All I was thinking of was August and I thought, 'She's not going to have a mum'.

‌



“I couldn't handle that. I did not want her to grow up without a mum." Stewart described the great white that mauled her as a "monster" and said: "Its face was horrific. I will never forget. It was holding on to my leg.. I just thought, 'I've got to fight it and do everything I can to be here'."

‌



View 4 Images Leah Stewart described the shark's face as 'horrific' (Image: GoFundMe)

Major update issued on boy injured in crocodile enclosure zoo horror READ MORE :

Stewart, a teacher, was in a coma for a fortnight after the attack and underwent operations including the amputation of much of her left arm.

She felt she had been given "a second chance at life", she said, and had spent the past two months healing and slowly returning to normal life. A GoFundMe campaign set up after the attack has raised £300,000 for her support.

‌



View 4 Images She was attacked by a great white shark (Image: Discovery Channel )

The attack has prompted New South Wales to introduce drone patrols to monitor sharks. If one is spotted, operators sound an alarm ordering swimmers to shore. After the attack the off-duty lifeguard who saved Leah revealed she thought she had felt a dolphin before being bitten.

Charlie Verco, 25, was paddle boarding about 100 metres from Leah, when the attack occurred at Coogee Beach on June 13th.

‌



Leah was swimming about 30 metres from shore when she was mauled by a great white shark, with Charlie paddling towards the shark before helping the mother out of the water.

View 4 Images Leah Stewart talks about surviving shark attack (Image: Facebook)

Speaking on the Straight Talk podcast Charlie said it was not clear immediately before the attack that a shark was in the water. He said: “I actually found out that she felt the shark before she saw it and said it felt like a wetsuit material and she thought it was a dolphin, looked around and saw that it was a shark and that was when she started screaming.”

Article continues below

Despite paddling towards danger he said he thought his large paddleboard “would probably frighten the shark and scare it off.”

But those thoughts changed when he saw the size of the great white. I was paddling over with that kind of intention, still pretty scared, still pretty hesitant,” he said.

“I eventually saw the shark come out of the water. I saw the dorsal fin, saw the back, saw the tail, and I saw the size of it… this thing's a pretty solid animal.”

News.title: Fears for King of Norway as Palace confirm his ‘health has deteriorated’
News.content:
Fears for King of Norway as Palace confirm his ‘health has deteriorated’

King Harald of Norway’s health has worsened in recent weeks, after he was rushed to hospital and shared he was on leave from his royal duties

View 4 Images King Harald of Norway is Europe's oldest reigning monarch (Image: Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Ima)

Norway’s King Harald has been hospitalised after a major health scare, with the Norwegian Palace confirming his ‘health has deteriorated’.

‌



The King, 89, who is Europe's oldest reigning monarch, was taken to the National Hospital in Oslo last week with a rare condition called haemolytic anaemia, which is when the immune system attacks red blood cells.

‌



As a result of the disorder, he was placed on sick leave from his royal duties, with his son and heir to the throne, Crown Prince Haakon, acting as regent. The Norwegian Royal Family issued an urgent statement on Sunday with an update on the monarch’s health.

‌



View 4 Images King Harald's health has deteriorated, the Norwegian Palace has confirmed (Image: Getty Images)

The statement read: "His Majesty the King's health deteriorated over the weekend. The King is receiving antibiotics for a bacterial infection in his blood, and has responded to this treatment."

They added: "His condition is stable. His Majesty will remain at Oslo University Hospital (Rikshospitalet) and is on sick leave until further notice." Many members of the Norwegian Royal Family have been seen visiting the hospital.

‌



The Palace confirmed the King’s condition within the last few weeks, saying he had "been treated with cortisone for the blood disease haemolytic anaemia. This has led to fluid accumulation in the body that requires treatment in hospital."

The disorder typically results in fatigue and breathlessness. The sole cause of the condition is not always obvious, but it can be caused by infections, other autoimmune conditions or certain drugs.

View 4 Images The monarch has been battling a rare condition called haemolytic anaemia (Image: Getty Images)

‌



King Harald, who has been on the throne since 1991, has suffered a series of health issues in the past. In April 2024, Norway's royal household said that the King would make a ‘permanent reduction’ to his public engagements ‘out of consideration for his age’.

That year, the king had been fitted with a pacemaker after falling ill on holiday in Malaysia. King Harald was also taken to hospital while on holiday in Tenerife in February after a health issue.

As a result of the King’s health, his wife, Queen Sonja, will now undertake a series of royal engagements, due to take place on September 1 and 2, on her own while her husband remains in hospital. Harald and Sonja are due to celebrate their 58th wedding anniversary on Saturday.

‌



King Harald is not the only member of the Norwegian Royal Family who has been battling major health conditions recently, as his daughter-in-law, Crown Princess Mette-Marit, is still recovering from a lung transplant.

View 4 Images Both King Harald and his daughter-in-law Mette-Marit have had difficult battles with their health (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The princess, who is married to Crown Prince Haakon, underwent a lung transplant in June as she continued to battle pulmonary fibrosis, which had worsened in recent months following her diagnosis with the disease in 2018.

In July, she announced she had been discharged from hospital following her major surgery, as she issued an emotional statement thanking healthcare workers for their support.

According to Are Holm, Head of the Department of Respiratory Medicine at Oslo University Hospital Rikshospitalet, the 52-year-old royal’s condition is “as good as can be expected”, adding that her rehabilitation will be closely monitored over the coming months.
