News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes calls out three Man Utd stars for Hull embarrassment as he tells Bruno Fernandes ‘keep your mouth shut’
Sports.content:
PAUL SCHOLES has slammed a number of Manchester United stars following the club’s embarrassing opening weekend defeat to Hull.

The Red Devils were stunned by two set-piece goals from the newly promoted outfit – the first time they have ever lost to a promoted side on opening day.



Some of the players chose to air their frustrations after the match, with captain Bruno Fernandes being especially vocal about his side’s short-comings.

He said: “Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to them.



“We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.”

But Scholes was none too impressed by the skipper’s comments, and slammed Fernandes and another United star for their own part in the shocking result.



Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite, Scholes said of the comments: “I’d be interested to know what (Fernandes) means by that. What mistakes were they giving set-piece goals away?

“Especially when you perform the way he did as well, I think it’s probably best to keep your mouth shut, because he didn’t have his best performance either, and there was quite a few of them like that.

Paddy McGuinness chimed in to add: “Luke Shaw said they could have been better prepared as well.”

To which Scholes responded: “Luke Shaw always says something.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“That’s a slight on your staff, that’s a slight on your manager. If one of your players was saying that, f***ing hell you’d have him in Monday morning wouldn’t you, ‘what do you mean by that?'”

The pair were not the only United stars that Scholes singled out. He and co-host Dion Dublin were perplexed by Harry Maguire‘s role in Hull’s first goal.

The England international appeared to mark Noussair Mazraoui rather than an opposition player in the box, allowing Semi Ajayi to pounce on a rebound which either man could possibly have cleared if they were not in each other’s way.

Scholes said: “I think he’s (Maguire) just lost his bearings or something, I don’t know. I don’t think he’s looking at the players, he’s looking at the ball, isn’t he?



“The only thing I can think is that he’s lost his bearings and he’s looking at the ball and he could feel somebody in front of him, and he’s just gone like that (hugged him).

Dublin added: “It’s an odd one because if he hadn’t had that instinct, then he might have been able to stop the goal or kick the ball away, but he just sort of froze and looked and he’s hugging his mate and he’s gone, ‘They’re gonna score in a minute!’

Scholes even called for Maguire to break down the moment himself, adding: “It doesn’t look good, does it? I’d like to hear him explain it.”

Sports.title: ‘Can’t focus on anything else’ – Fans in stitches as Gary Neville’s baggy trousers mocked by Jamie Carragher on live TV
Sports.content:
JAMIE CARRAGHER left viewers in stitches after taking a dig at Gary Neville’s wardrobe.

The pair of Sky Sports stalwarts were back on football fans’ screens for the first Monday Night Football show of the season.



However, one key points of discussion ended up being Carragher poking fun at his colleagues attire.

Carragher, 48, said: “Can I add one more to watch?”



The Liverpool icon then turned to Neville and pointed at his trousers before saying: “Will you wear them trousers again?”

The quip saw Neville erupt into laughter before explaining that he had gone for a wide trouser fit.

Carragher joked: “He looks like Frank Worthington.”

Manchester United legend Neville then hit back by saying: “What you’ll find is Carra will start wearing these in about two or three years. He’ll catch up.”

The 51-year-old then stood up to show off his trousers, adding: “I went shopping on Saturday in London. This guy styled me.

“I’ll tell you what I think they’re pretty cool. I like these.”

Sports.title: European giant rocked as ‘entire board RESIGNS at emergency meeting’ following disastrous result
Sports.content:
THE entire FK Partizan board have resigned after the club lost its third game in a row.

Serbian giants Partizan are sitting 12th in the league after five matches with just one win after going down 3-1 to Mladost Lucani on Sunday.



And head coach Sasa Ilic QUIT immediately after – but he has since been talked into staying on for one more game.

The boss was told to take charge of Thursday’s crucial Conference League play-off second leg at home to Getafe.



Spaniards Getafe won the first game 3-1 last week and Ilic will remain to try and turn things around.

And other key members will be out no matter what the result is – including president Rasim Ljajic.



He held an EMERGENCY meeting with general director Danko Lazovic and Ilic after the Mladost defeat.

Head of football Radosav Petrovic was also there and is set to exit as well.

A statement confirmed: “The FK Partizan Management Board takes full responsibility for the results achieved.”

Elections for the next leadership team will be held between September 21 and 25 during the extended international break.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Partizan are eight-time Serbian league winners, with another eight in the Yugoslavia top division with Serbia and Montenegro, and 11 Yugoslav First League titles before that.

They have won 16 domestic cups as well and are historic rivals to the country’s biggest side, Red Star Belgrade.

But after finishing third last season, they have already lost four times in all competition this time round.

Partizan are just three points above bottom and have already had two red cards.

They even had a man sent off in their final friendly of the summer – a 4-1 win.

Sports.title: Do Carabao Cup 2nd round ties go to extra time or straight to penalties if it ends as a draw after 90 minutes?
Sports.content:
SEVERAL Premier League clubs begin their Carabao Cup campaigns in the second round.

English giants Chelsea, Tottenham, Newcastle and Everton are among the 11 top-flight sides without European commitments, which means they enter the competition at this stage.



Some second round ties look too close to call and could still be level at the end of normal time.

If the match ends all square, the question at the front of everyone’s mind is whether there is extra time and penalties.



SunSport brings you all the information you need.

Do Carabao Cup 2nd round ties go to extra time or straight to penalties if it ends as a draw after 90 minutes?

Carabao Cup second round ties go straight to penalties if the score is level after 90 minutes.



Ahead of the 2018/19 season, organisers scrapped extra time to reduce “additional fatigue issues” following a vote by English Football League clubs.

Extra time is used only in the Carabao Cup in the second leg of the semi-finals (if the aggregate score is level) and in the final.

What happened in last year’s Carabao Cup final?

Manchester City are the Carabao Cup holders after they beat Arsenal 2-0 in last year’s final.

Nico O’Reilly scored twice in four second-half minutes to fire his side to Wembley glory.



City’s triumph meant that Pep Guardiola became the first manager to win the League Cup five times.

The legendary gaffer left his post at the Etihad at the end of last season.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup third-round draw explained including 'pre-draw' for Premier League giants
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup third-round draw explained including 'pre-draw' for Premier League giants

European fixtures for several Premier League sides has thrown the next round of the Carabao Cup into chaos, forcing the EFL to get creative with the upcoming draw

View 2 Images The Carabao Cup third-round draw is set to take place this week (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

The EFL have been forced to adapt the draw for the third round of the Carabao Cup after European fixtures threw a major spanner in the works.

‌



The draw will take place on Wednesday evening, following the conclusion of Preston vs Everton, on Sky Sports. It will come before all the second-round ties are concluded, with Chelsea vs Luton and Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon both taking place on Thursday night.

‌



That is just one minor confusion. It is the eight Premier League sides who are set to compete in the Champions League or Europa League this season which makes things difficult for the EFL.

‌



Arsenal, Aston Villa, Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United are all in the Champions League, while Crystal Palace, Bournemouth and Sunderland will feature in the Europa League. Brighton could still qualify for the Conference League via the qualifiers, that competition doesn't begin until October so won't clash.

Fixtures for the Champions League and Europa League in September, set for the week beginning September 7 and September 14 respectively, will clash with the third round of the Carabao Cup. The EFL have therefore decided to introduce new conditions for the draw to ensure that the aforementioned clubs cannot face each other in the third round.

They have also introduced a "pre-draw", which will take place on Sky Sports before Preston vs Everton. That will be used to determined whether the Premier League sides involved in European competitions will be drawn at home or away in the main draw.

The EFL explained in a statement: "In the main draw, to be conducted after the round two tie, the first eight ties will involve those Champions League and Europa League clubs, with their home or away position already having been decided, and each will be drawn against a club from a separate bowl containing the remaining teams. Once those eight ties have been drawn, the final eight ties will be drawn as normal."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso needs to follow Pep Guardiola and Mikel Arteta with ruthless goalkeeper decision
Sports.content:
Even though he was part of a winning team that produced a very encouraging first Premier League display under Xabi Alonso, Robert Sanchez would be well-advised to stay away from social media for a while. Oh, and not catch up with the thoughts of Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher after Chelsea’s 3-2 win at Fulham.

“We have to be careful about criticising players or goalkeepers, but …,” and you can guess the rest from Neville. The Sky Sports pundits were scathing in their criticism of Sanchez and were supported by the vast majority of Chelsea supporters who posted their views online.

The pile-on was a little over the top. Sanchez was certainly at fault for Fulham’s first goal and would have hoped to do a little better ahead of their second. But the all-round defending for Gonzalo Garcia’s goal was shoddy, to say the least.

Yet add these opening-day lapses to last season’s sprinkling of mistakes, and the issue is as painfully clear as many are making out. Without European football to clog up their calendar and with a reshaped squad that suddenly looks balanced - not to mention a high-calibre, proven manager at the helm - Chelsea should be title contenders.

But contending will be a lot tougher if Sanchez is the first-choice keeper. That is the stark reality. And that is not just based on the errors at Craven Cottage.

Sure, they are well-blessed with keepers, but 28-year-old Sanchez has only three caps for Spain and did not make the squad for the World Cup. That tells you something.

View 3 Images Aaron Ramsdale was ruthlessly replaced as Arsenal's first-choice keeper in the summer of 2023 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Alonso has a duty of care to a player who is already coming in for some fierce, personal criticism, but it goes without saying that managers need to be ruthless to succeed at the highest level. Being ruthless with keepers is particularly crucial.

The best recent example is Mikel Arteta replacing Aaron Ramsdale with David Raya at the start of the 2023/24 season. Don’t forget, Arteta’s decision was not based on Ramsdale making the sort of notable errors that Sanchez has made.

Ramsdale had just signed a new long-term contract and had been named in the PFA Team of the Year after the 2022/23 season. Arteta’s brutal decisiveness took a little while to pay dividends, but it certainly has.

The same proved true in the summer of 2016 after Pep Guardiola told Joe Hart he would not be the goalkeeping future of Manchester City. At the time, Hart was a keeper who had two Premier League titles, an FA Cup, two League Cups and 63 England caps to his name (Guardiola’s decision meant Hart won only 12 more caps).

‌



View 3 Images Xabi Alonso refused to criticise Robert Sanchez after the Chelsea keeper's display against Fulham (Image: Jacques Feeney/Getty Images)

One of the most famous examples of one-off ruthlessness came after Manchester United and Crystal Palace had played out a thrilling 3-3 draw in the 1990 FA Cup final. For the replay, Alex Ferguson dropped Jim Leighton - his trusted friend and keeper from their Aberdeen days - and played Les Sealey, winning the game 1-0 to collect his first trophy as United manager.

Considering their positive attitude towards the transfer market, it is a surprise that Chelsea and Alonso began their Premier League campaign without recruiting a fresh goalkeeping option. When it became clear James Trafford would be leaving Manchester City, Chelsea should have been in the mix for his signature.

The problem now, of course, is that clubs will be aware of Chelsea’s needs and will demand top dollar. But there are options out there. Diogo Costa has a £51million release clause in his Porto contract, while Borussia Dortmund might be tempted to cash in on Gregor Kobel.

‌



After only one game of the Premier League season, it is harsh on Sanchez, who still has a good career ahead of him. But whoever Chelsea decide to pursue, they have to pursue someone before the transfer window closes - otherwise, an unlikely title challenge becomes very unlikely.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola's behaviour speaks volumes as Liverpool transfer chances emerge
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola's behaviour speaks volumes as Liverpool transfer chances emerge

Liverpool are still trying to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain before this summer transfer window ends, as new head coach Andoni Iraola wants wingers

View 2 Images Liverpool are determined to take Bradley Barcola to Anfield before the transfer window shuts (Image: LOU BENOIST, AFP via Getty Images)

Bradley Barcola and his entourage are not panicking about the length of negotiations between Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain as his transfer saga drags on. It is said they remain confident that both clubs will reach an agreement before the end of this summer transfer window at 11pm on 1 September.

‌



PSG have left Barcola out of the squad for their last two matches. The first was the French Super Cup, which they lost 1-0 to Lens. However, he was photographed training the day beforehand, and also attended the match.

‌



Barcola has not been involved for a fortnight since being an unused substitute in the UEFA Super Cup win over Aston Villa. PSG's only remaining match before the transfer deadline is on Friday night against Lille.

‌



All sides involved in Barcola transfer negotiations appear hopeful that a switch to Liverpool will be finalised during the final days of the summer window. The winger has been linked with the Reds in recent months, however, the process has required patience from all concerned, as several critical elements still need to fall into place.

The initial considerations for Liverpool focused on a genuine willingness to pursue a deal. With Barcola entering the final two years of his Parc des Princes contract, he needed to signal his readiness to leave to force PSG into a decision.

Liverpool will ignore Jamie Carragher's desperate transfer plea with focus elsewhere READ MORE :

Virgil van Dijk sends Liverpool chiefs transfer message with Andoni Iraola in agreement READ MORE :

Once that became apparent, the French and European champions faced the question of whether a sale would best serve their interests in maximising the player's market value. This decision subsequently came to pass.

‌



Liverpool then needed to establish themselves as the leading contenders to land Barcola, which happened swiftly, before PSG set about identifying replacements in the transfer market to bolster their own attacking ranks. Everything fell into place for the Reds, who then faced the most daunting hurdle of all: club-to-club negotiations.

Les Parisiens placed a hefty price tag on the winger, creating a significant gap between the two clubs that needed to be closed before any deal could be struck. PSG knocked back initial bids as Liverpool looked to formalise their interest, with talks continuing deep into the final week of the transfer window.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has not been in a Paris Saint-Germain matchday squad since the UEFA Super Cup (Image: SOPA Images, SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It now appears the drawn-out saga is at last moving towards a conclusion that works for all involved, with widespread expectation that Barcola will ultimately complete his move to Anfield. According to a report from L'Equipe, Liverpool are readying a final bid for the winger that they are confident PSG will accept, following a narrowing of the valuation gap between the two clubs over recent weeks.

It is understood that Barcola and his representatives are growing increasingly optimistic that a deal will be struck, with 'nobody in panic mode', despite the apparent lack of progress thus far. There is an expectation that the transfer fee will exceed the Ligue Un record for a sale to a foreign club, surpassing both Ayyoub Bouaddi's impending switch to Manchester City this summer and Neymar's move to Al-Hilal in 2023.

‌



The exact final sum remains unclear, with those details to be finalised in the dying days of the summer transfer window. Nevertheless, the deal would significantly strengthen Liverpool's attacking arsenal.

This marks just one of multiple expected transactions in Liverpool's late transfer flurry, with attention still focused on Minteh to bolster the right-wing choices at Andoni Iraola's disposal. Meanwhile, Cody Gakpo remains the subject of rumours regarding a potential exit. All of which suggests a frantic final week in the market for the Reds, with substantial business to be completed both incoming and outgoing at the club.

Sports.title: Liverpool will ignore Jamie Carragher's desperate transfer plea with focus elsewhere
Sports.content:
Liverpool will ignore Jamie Carragher's desperate transfer plea with focus elsewhere

Liverpool are prioritising the signing of attacking wide players in the final few days of the summer transfer window, much to the annoyance of Jamie Carragher

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher wants a new midfielder at Liverpool (Image: Sky Sports)

Liverpool will not sign a central midfielder in the final few days of the summer transfer window, despite a passionate plea from Jamie Carragher.

‌



The Reds kicked off their Premier League campaign with a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Sunday. Dominik Szoboszlai's last-gasp penalty earned Andoni Iraola's side a point after conceding to Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock.

‌



Iraola fielded Szoboszlai in midfield alongside Ryan Gravenberch at St James' Park, with Alexis Mac Allister coming off the bench in the second half. Carragher was alarmed by how open the away side were on the break, with Newcastle ripping through Liverpool's defences with their pace.

‌



Liverpool have so far brought in defenders Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo and winger Victor Munoz this summer. They are now chasing Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh and Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola before the window closes on September 1.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The Athletic reports that, despite selling Curtis Jones to Inter Milan for £25.7million plus £4.3m in add-ons, they are not planning to bring in another midfielder. Academy graduate Trey Nyoni, 19, is considered ready to step up and add to his 20 first-team appearances.

Fellow midfielder James McConnell could be sent out on loan to the Championship to further reduce numbers in the middle of the pitch, where Wataru Endo is also available.

After tearing apart Liverpool's midfield, and particularly Gravenberch for his failure to track Willock for Newcastle's second goal, Carragher made his feelings clear on Sky Sports.

‌



View 2 Images Ryan Gravenberch's performance against Newcastle was criticised by Jamie Carragher (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

He said: “Liverpool need someone alongside Gravenberch. It doesn't necessarily need to be a player who can't get on the ball and he's just tackling and stopping players. If you play for one of the top teams in the world, you need to be able to get hold of the ball.

“But I want someone who can run. Szoboszlai has to go to the No 10. I've always seen this coming. When people are saying [Wirtz] has got to go to No 10, that means Szoboszlai's got to be in the team and he's not a central midfield player.

‌



“I thought this would come up in six weeks, I think it's coming up right now. I don't see where he fits in at all, really. What's Iraola going to do with Wirtz? You can't keep going with it; it's not working,

“It didn't work last season. Liverpool last season conceded 78 goals, 53 in the Premier League, the most they've ever conceded in the Premier League. And all of a sudden it's all about buying wingers?"

Sports.title: Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates

Bruno Fernandes has so often been the hero for Manchester United, but the Reds skipper has been the subject of ire from club icon Paul Scholes

View 3 Images Paul Scholes was not happy with Bruno Fernandes' recent comments (Image: YouTube/The Good, the Bad and the Football podcast)

Bruno Fernandes has been told to "shut his mouth" by Paul Scholes after the Manchester United skipper criticised his team-mates. Fernandes blasted United for repeating the clumsy errors they repeatedly made last season after their 2-0 defeat to Hull City.

‌



The shock result was only Michael Carrick's second Premier League defeat as United manager, but there is already an inquisition about the Reds' transfer business. They spent £85million on midfield duo Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, who were both hauled off in the second half as United looked for a route back into the game.

‌



After Fernandes' cutting honesty about how he and his team-mates played against Hull, Scholes expressed his unhappiness with the Portuguese ace's comments.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

When quizzed about the United captain's criticism, Scholes, speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite, said: "When you perform the way he did as well, I think it's probably best to keep your mouth shut, because he didn't have his best performance either."

Following the defeat to the relegation favourites, Fernandes told TNT Sports: "Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

‌



"We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these type of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.

View 3 Images Fernandes' comments were not received well by Paul Scholes (Image: PAUL ELLIS, AFP via Getty Images)

"We knew before the game set-pieces would be a big part of their game. They played all pre-season with a back four but had a five against us for some height, for these moments. The most frustrating thing is that we lost the game."

‌



Fernandes slotted alongside Tielemans and Santos in United's midfield, which endured a torrid afternoon against the Tigers. Reflecting on the outcome, Scholes does not believe any of the new additions have been an upgrade, stating: "You speak about recruitment wise and I saw the central midfield the other day and I thought 'that is no better than last'.

"I mean, when you're recruiting players and looking for a different team, you think, 'I've got to get better.' To me, on Saturday, that wasn't better than Kobbie Mainoo and Casemiro together."

View 3 Images Hull were by far the better team against United (Image: George Wood, Getty Images)

‌



United are hopeful of shortly unveiling Carlos Baleba as their latest signing. The Brighton & Hove Albion star appears set to become the third central midfielder to arrive at the club this campaign.

Baleba is anticipated to complete a £70m switch to United, which would push the Reds' total spending on central midfielders to £135m. United welcome Ipswich Town to Old Trafford in their next Premier League outing on Sunday, August 30.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso's four-word message to Robert Sanchez after Chelsea goalkeeper's nightmare
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso's four-word message to Robert Sanchez after Chelsea goalkeeper's nightmare

Chelsea kicked off their Premier League campaign - and the Xabi Alonso era - with a 3-2 win over Fulham, but Robert Sanchez's performance in goal left a lot to be desired

View 2 Images Robert Sanchez was arguably at fault for both Fulham goals (Image: AFP / Getty Images)

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has encouraged Robert Sanchez to "relax and carry on" despite his dreadful start to the Premier League season.

‌



The Blues picked up a 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday night, with Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers all scoring at Craven Cottage. But while their attack looked impressive, there was an obvious issue at the other end.

‌



Sanchez was beaten at his near post by Josh King's low effort and he was also at fault for Fulham's second goal, pushing out a shot for Gonzalo Garcia to head in a rebound.

‌



The Spanish goalkeeper's erratic performances are nothing new, with mistakes a feature of his three-year Chelsea career. But Alonso refused to criticise his goalkeeper when speaking to reporters post-match.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It's about the team, it's not about the individual," Alonso said when asked about Sanchez's mistakes. "The first goal, we can do better to defend, we can do better to avoid, but it's part of the game. We need to accept and to learn. This is going to be a process.

"All the lines, from the strikers, the midfielders, the defence, the goalkeepers, we want to do better in everything. The goal was to start good, and we've been able to start well. Relax and carry on."

Sanchez has been Chelsea's number one goalkeeper since joining for £20million from Brighton three years ago. He has made 112 appearances, keeping his place in the side in spite of Chelsea's busy nature in the transfer market.

‌



View 2 Images Xabi Alonso dismissed concerns about his goalkeeper (Image: Jacques Feeney/Getty Images)

Mike Penders, a 21-year-old goalkeeper who has never made an appearance for Chelsea, was on the bench against Fulham. The Belgian joined last summer from Genk and spent last season on loan at sister club Strasbourg. Filip Jorgensen, who was the back-up last season, has been sent to Strasbourg on loan for the 2026/27 season.

Both Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville have urged Chelsea to sign a new goalkeeper before the transfer window closes on September 1 to replace Sanchez.

‌



"I do think [there are] concerns defensively," Carragher said on Sky Sports after the Fulham game. "They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it's going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight."

Neville added: "I don't know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It's a problem."

Sports.title: What is the reality of Villa's finances ahead of Deadline Day?
Sports.content:
All of this is a far cry from the euphoria of Istanbul in May, and that is what adds to the feeling of bemusement about how significant the changes have been to Aston Villa's squad and how quickly it has occurred.

Last season was their most successful since 1982, when they won the old European Cup.

This time round, it was a Europa League win and a fourth-place Premier League finish - each of those achievements would have been enough to guarantee the riches and prestige of Champions League football.

Unai Emery was lauded as a hero by Villa fans even before last spring's spectacular, and rightly so.

He has won the Europa League title five times with three different clubs. A key question now is whether his downbeat assessment following the humbling by Brighton is indicative of a wider concern.

Clearly, Emery was upset with Ollie Watkins, and it currently seems a tall order for the striker to be reintegrated into the Villa squad, having made his desire to leave clear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Unai Emery was short of words when asked about the future of Ollie Watkins and then after the match said to find out we should call the striker

But more worrying is the overriding sense that Emery is struggling with the lack of options he has at his disposal right now.

After all that he has achieved at the club, his reward has been widespread disruption within the squad after four key player departures, potentially more to come, and limited finances.

Emery described it as having "had an intelligent market", amid efforts by the club to strengthen the squad before the deadline. "We know where we are and we know what we want to do again for the next year," he said.

There is mitigation for Villa's bosses, however, who have been frustrated by PSR rules, which they feel have been an ambition killer and stalled their progress.

The switch to Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) rules this season has only added to that and caused deeper resentment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports explains the new financial Squad Cost Ratio rules that Premier League clubs will have to adhere to this season

As regulars in European competition now, they are limited to spending 70 per cent of their football revenue on transfer fees and player wages.

Remember, they have already been fined twice by UEFA recently, being hit with a £9.5m penalty last year and a £19.4m fine in June, although £13m of that was suspended after Villa came to a settlement agreement.

That means, inevitably, Villa are a club that has to generate income from player trading in order to buy new talent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher discuss the outgoings of Aston Villa this transfer window and how much of an impact this could have on their season

The proof of that is in the figures from sales over the last three years; Villa have made over £410m selling the likes of Douglas Luiz, Jhon Duran, Jacob Ramsey and Moussa Diaby, before this summer's sale of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne.

Should Emiliano Martinez and Ollie Watkins follow, that number will be close to the half-a-billion mark, in terms of funds generated.

It is a big ask for Emery to see the castle that he has built taken down keystone by keystone, knowing he has to rebuild again. Last summer, the transfer upheaval contributed to the director of football Monchi leaving the club.

Importantly, Villa currently feel confident their manager is secure. After all, his contract has another three seasons to run, following the bumper new five-year deal he signed in May 2024.

But many of the biggest clubs in Europe have noticed with admiration the job Emery has done at Villa Park, and he will always be on the shortlist of the top clubs for as long as he keeps doing such a stellar job under the circumstances.

Sports.title: 'Stupid mistakes' - Root 'hacked off' by latest off-field incident
Sports.content:
A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.

England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.

Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.

"In terms of the incident itself, obviously with the regulator, there's not a lot I can say on it. It's in their hands now.

"I've spoken to Brydon when I first found out; my first concern was for him as a person. In my time in the dressing room, you obviously develop personal relationships with players.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn when I say he's been very upset and has been very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

Image: Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub in Derby

"It's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact that we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the day three of the first Test between England and Pakistan as Joe Root's side cruised to an innings victory at Headingley.

'We have to earn a lot of trust back'

Asked if English cricket had an image problem, Root, who previously called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, said: "We have an opportunity going forward.

"Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.

"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.

"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain praise England's winning fast bowler combinations during the three-day victory over Pakistan in first Test.

"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen [Fleming], and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."

Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.

"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.

"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.

"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

Sports.title: Baumgardner to face undefeated Turhan as blockbuster Dubois showdown nears
Sports.content:
Alycia Baumgardner will move up a division to fight Elif Nur Turhan for her IBF lightweight world title on November 8 in a seismic move that brings a blockbuster showdown with Caroline Dubois a step closer.

Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.

"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

"I do not want to lose either. As two boxers sharing a 'win at all costs' mentality, we guarantee a fierce, relentless battle where everything is left on the line. Two warriors, one fight and only one winner."

Victory for Baumgardner would see her become a two-weight world champion in the same division as Dubois, who holds the WBC and WBO titles.

The 32-year-old is set to be ringside for Dubois' clash with Amelia Moore on Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

Since December, Dubois has been vociferous in calling out Baumgardner, and those calls have only intensified since she beat Terri Harper to unify the division in April.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Baumgardner dismissed the prospects of facing Caroline Dubois after her win over Bo Mi Re Shin. Instead, the fighter called out Katie Taylor and Amanda Serrano

Baumgardner has maintained that, despite her status as a unified world champion, Dubois has yet to reach the level required for her to entertain a fight between them.

But should Baumgardner inflict a first career defeat on Turhan, all roads will surely lead to a blockbuster unification bout with Dubois, where the winner would move to within one victory of becoming undisputed champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dubois is determined to fight Baumgardner sooner rather than later

The co-main event on November 8 will see England's Ellie Scotney fight the undefeated Tiara Brown over 10 rounds for the WBC featherweight world title.

Former undisputed super bantamweight champion Scotney will step up to 126lbs as she bids to become a two-weight world champion.

"MVPW-07 is one of the biggest championship events in boxing history, with four back-to-back world title fights, bringing together eight elite fighters from around the world with belts at stake in every match-up," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

Sports.title: Littler and Van Gerwen to headline World Series of Darts Finals
Sports.content:
Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price will headline a packed field competing for a top prize of £100,000 at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals.

The event, which has a £450,000 prize pot, will return to the AFAS Live in Amsterdam and is set to take place between September 17-20.

Reigning champion Van Gerwen will be out to defend his title on home soil after he bested Littler in last year's final to scoop an £80,000 cheque at last year's event.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael van Gerwen ended his two-year wait for a top-level PDC title by beating Luke Littler at last year's event

Van Gerwen has been in excellent form on the circuit this year, having already won the Bahrain Darts Masters in January and the Nordic Darts Masters in June.

He also came close to winning the inaugural Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January, but was bested by Littler 8-5 in the final.

World Matchplay champion Littler enters the tournament as the third seed, while Price, who was beaten by the 19-year-old in the final at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool, is the second seed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler comes into the event after winning the Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January

Luke Humphries also joins the 32-player field as the fourth seed, after he claimed victory at the US Darts masters in June, while New Zealand Darts Masters winner Jonny Clayton and Australian Darts Masters champion James Wade are seeded sixth and seventh, respectively.

Gian van Veen and Stephen Bunting, seeded fifth and eighth, make up the final seeded players on the list.

Those inside the top 24 of the final World Series rankings will gain a berth to play in Amsterdam.

Australian Brody Klinge, who was beaten by Wade in the final of the Australian Darts Masters, will make his debut at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Sports.title: 'Not the best version of me' - Hamilton regrets frustrated Dutch GP comments
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says he didn't present "the best version" of himself when criticising his Ferrari team over the radio and in television interviews at the Dutch Grand Prix.

Hamilton sounded irate in a series of radio messages sent when he was being held up by team-mate Charles Leclerc despite the pair being on different strategies during the race in Zandvoort.

The seven-time world champion felt as though the lost time ultimately cost him a podium as he finished fourth just behind George Russell having been unable to overtake the Mercedes in an exciting finale.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix.

Hamilton, who joined Ferrari from Mercedes in 2025, doubled down on his criticism of his team after the race when he compared the Italian squad's hesitation to get Leclerc out of his way to the Silver Arrows decisively ordering Russell to let his team-mate, championship leader Kimi Antonelli, pass him later in the race.

Reflecting on the weekend an in Instagram post on Monday, Hamilton said: "I've listened back to some of my radio and TV comments. In the heat of the moment frustration can come out, especially when you care as deeply as I do.

"But that wasn't the best version of me. I take responsibility for that, and I'll be better."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton outlined his frustrations after a fourth-place finish at the Dutch Grand Prix.

The result saw Hamilton's deficit to Antonelli at the top of the drivers' standings increase to 59 points, with the Ferrari driver also dropping to third behind Russell, who has the same number of points as his former team-mate but has won more races this season.

Despite the race - won by McLaren's Lando Norris - representing a third successive grand prix for Hamilton without a podium, the 41-year-old insisted the fight for the title "is absolutely still on".

He continued: "That passion comes from believing in this team, the people in it, and what we're building together. The direction is clear. The belief is there. And the fight is absolutely still on.

"Thank you for sticking with us and with me. We'll keep building, keep pushing and keep fighting."

Ferrari continued what has been an impressive development drive throughout the season by bringing a new floor and diffuser to Zandvoort, with the team's efforts drawing praise from Hamilton.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The Fast And The Curious podcast, Betty Glover, Christian Hewgill and Greg James reflect on their favourite radio messages from the Dutch GP.

"I'm incredibly proud of everyone back at the factory who continues to bring updates, find performance and push us forward," Hamilton said.

"To the team at the track, thank you. The commitment and effort never go unnoticed. We still have work to do, particularly over one lap, but we'll keep digging in, learning and improving together."

Rosberg urges Ferrari improvement

Hamilton's former team-mate Nico Rosberg urged Ferrari to improve their execution of races as he believes they have the potential for "much better results".

With Leclerc finishing a place behind Hamilton in fifth, Ferrari's deficit to Mercedes at the top of the Constructors' Championship grew to 87 points.

"Ferrari have been top five all the time but there's a little bit of the feeling after every weekend of 'what could have been'," the 2016 world champion and Sky Sports F1 pundit said after Sunday's race.

"Even in the last couple of races - Hungary I felt [Lewis] could have won that if things had gone his way and, this weekend, they were a bit more off the pace, but only in qualifying. In the race they were fast.

"They keep on just not maximising weekends and that's how Lewis seems a bit frustrated, and also Charles. Both of them.

"It's very little things that seem to add up all the time. So they've got to improve that and on the execution side just nail it because they can really, just with that, get much better results."

Sports.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner York arrested
Sports.content:
Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences

Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools

Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.

York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution , according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.

"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.

They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.

When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.

Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.

Sports.title: NRL to allow Arrow to reach Rabbitohs century after MND retirement
Sports.content:
The NRL is planning an exception to its rules to allow Jai Arrow to reach the 100-game milestone for the South Sydney Rabbitohs after retiring earlier this year due to a motor neurone disease diagnosis.

MND Australia describes it as an umbrella term for a group of progressive neurological conditions in which the motor neurones degenerate. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the most common form, and is often called Lou Gehrig's disease.

As part of an agreement with the Rabbitohs, the NRL granted South Sydney special dispensation to include Arrow, 31, as an extra player on Tuesday's official team list and an additional interchange in their rotation for Saturday's game against the Gold Coast Titans.

A similar dispensation will be granted for South Sydney's final regular-season game against the Sydney Roosters.

According to the NRL, Arrow will get dressed in South Sydney playing kit on both matchdays, join the Rabbitohs in the dressing room, lead the team onto the field, become the team's first interchange within seconds of the opening whistle without taking part in any play, and then remain on the interchange bench in his playing kit for the rest of the game.

It will take Arrow's tally to 180 career NRL games and 100 for the Rabbitohs, in addition to his representative appearances for Queensland in the annual State of Origin series.

Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys said it was a chance for the sport to be a "conduit to bring out the best of humanity".

Image: Arrow has announced his immediate retirement from rugby league after being diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease

"This thoughtful gesture by the South Sydney Rabbitohs shows the true heart of our game," V'landys said. "Jai has inspired millions of people around the world with the courage and strength he has shown in his fight with MND. He is not only a great player, but an extraordinary person.

"Reaching 100 games for the Rabbitohs is a special achievement, one that Jai, his family and everyone who has supported him should be incredibly proud of. The entire rugby league community stands with Jai and is honoured to celebrate this remarkable milestone with him."

Rugby league star Rob Burrow and Scotland rugby union great Doddie Weir are among the high-profile sportsmen to have died from the illness in recent years.

Sports.title: WSL academy teams to play in third tier after FA approves controversial plan
Sports.content:
Four Women’s Super League academy sides will play in tier three of the pyramid from the 2027-28 season after the controversial proposal was approved by the Football Association’s board.

The change forms part of what the FA described as a package of reforms to the Women’s National League “designed to strengthen the women’s football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players”.

The FA said data showed that young English players were getting significantly fewer competitive minutes than their counterparts across Europe’s leading leagues.

Quick Guide How do I 

The FA said WNL clubs would receive central funding for the first time and that changes to the loan market would encourage clubs from the top two divisions to loan players to clubs in the third and fourth tiers.

The WSL academy teams will not be eligible for promotion and will be chosen against criteria to be developed in the coming months, the FA said. With the third tier split into two geographical regions, it is expected that two academies will be placed in the northern division and two in the southern.

Sue Day, director of women’s football at the FA, said: “For the game to continue moving forward, the FA Women’s National League must evolve alongside the professional game, and we need to create more opportunities for talented young English players to develop in senior football.”

Sports.title: Savinho seals £75m Spurs move from Manchester City – and changes name to Sávio
Sports.content:
Savinho has completed his £75m move to Tottenham from Manchester City and marked the beginning of a new chapter in his career by indicating that he wants to be known as Sávio from now on.

The Brazil winger, who will cost up to an additional £10m in add-ons, will have Sávio on the back of his shirt. The fee represents a record sale for City, who signed him from Troyes in 2024 for £30.8m.

The deal for Sávio takes Spurs’s summer spend to £304.5m and they are not finished. They are close to signing the City forward Omar Marmoush for somewhere between £50m and £75m. They are also monitoring Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.

The Spurs manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has been keen to add greater punch in his attacking line, a feeling that intensified after the team’s 3-0 defeat at Brentford on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

Sávio prefers to play off the right wing, where he can cut inside on to his stronger left foot. De Zerbi started the 18-year-old Mikey Moore on the right at Brentford. His other option in the position is Mohammed Kudus, who is “almost ready” to return, according to De Zerbi, from the thigh injury sustained in January.

Sávio had three goals and 13 assists in all competitions in his first season at City, 10 of the latter coming in the Premier League. He was less productive last time out with four goals and three assists in all competitions. In 53 Premier League appearances he has scored twice.

Quick Guide How do I 

“It’s taken a while but I’m very happy to be here,” the 22-year-old told the Spurs website. “As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.”

De Zerbi said: “Sávio is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity.”

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.
