The Pan-American Congress closes with a call for more equal north-south dialogue

24th Monday, August 2026 - 21:55 UTC Full article

“It is necessary to reframe the dialogue between the north and south of the Americas in more equal terms,” said the meeting's coordinator, David Adler, at the closing session held at the Teatro Solís

The third Pan-American Congress concluded on Sunday in Montevideo with a call to reframe relations between the north and south of the Americas on more equal terms. The forum, which brought together some 150 lawmakers, governors and former heads of state from fifteen countries, will hold its next edition in Brazil in 2027.

“It is necessary to reframe the dialogue between the north and south of the Americas in more equal terms,” said the meeting's coordinator, David Adler, at the closing session held at the Teatro Solís. Conclusions were organised around regional integration, peace and security, care policies and welfare systems.

The congress was marked by one notable absence: former Colombian president Gustavo Petro, who promoted the first edition, held in Bogotá in 2024. Organisers cancelled his participation as a precaution to avoid exposure to sanctions, since Petro has been listed since October 2025 by the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the US Treasury Department, along with the then first lady, his eldest son and his interior minister. The designation, administrative rather than judicial in character, cited an alleged role in illicit drug trafficking. There has been no trial or conviction, and the Colombian government at the time described it as political persecution.

Among the subjects debated was the militarisation of public security in several countries in the region. Brazilian senator Humberto Costa warned that the inclusion of two organisations from his country on the US list of terrorist groups affects national sovereignty and could serve as an argument for military intervention under the justification of combating drug trafficking. He called for particular attention to Brazil ahead of October's presidential elections.

US lawmakers present referred to the midterm elections due in November in their country. Representative Jesús García called for prioritising the wellbeing of working people and respect for the sovereignty of Latin American nations.

The gathering, held from Friday to Sunday with both public sessions and closed-door debates, also included an address by Macarena Gelman, granddaughter of Argentine poet Juan Gelman, whose identity was taken from her at birth during Argentina's dictatorship and who was located years later by the Grandmothers of the Plaza de Mayo. The figure of the late Uruguayan president José Mujica was repeatedly invoked in speeches.

The forum began in Bogotá in 2024 and held its second edition in Mexico City in 2025. With Brazil chosen as host, the meeting moves to the region's largest country in the year following its presidential elections.

World.title: Man detained in Buenos Aires after driving a stolen bus, saying it was his dream
World.content:
Man detained in Buenos Aires after driving a stolen bus, saying it was his dream

24th Monday, August 2026 - 21:44 UTC Full article

The situation came to light when the bus scraped another vehicle belonging to the same company

A man was detained on Sunday in the western part of the Buenos Aires metropolitan area after driving a city bus for several kilometres, having taken it without authorisation from a depot, following the line's regular route and picking up passengers at stops.

The episode began at around 6:30am at the depot operated by Empresa 216 in Pontevedra, in the district of Merlo. According to investigators' reconstruction, the man boarded a vehicle that was parked there and drove it away. He covered Pontevedra and central Morón, two districts of greater Buenos Aires, keeping to the established route and stopping to let passengers board, none of whom noticed anything irregular. He was wearing a shirt bearing the company logo.

The situation came to light when the bus scraped another vehicle belonging to the same company. Its driver alerted colleagues and, once it was confirmed the unit had left the depot without its assigned driver, a union representative filed a theft report at the police station.

A patrol car located the bus in southern Morón. An officer from the fourth precinct of Gervasio Pavón went to a stop a few metres from the station, raised his arm as though he were a passenger and, when the vehicle stopped, boarded, identified himself and told the driver he was under arrest.

The case is being handled by Prosecutor's Office No. 2 in Morón, headed by Fernando Capello, which ordered a psychiatric evaluation of the detainee to determine whether he is fit to face charges. On being detained, the man said: “I wanted to fulfil my dream of being a bus driver.” According to the newspaper Perfil, officers seized a knife from him. No injuries have been reported.

The bus sustained bodywork damage as a result of the collision and was handed to the company for repairs before returning to service. The detainee has not been publicly identified and has not been convicted.

Urban bus lines, known locally as colectivos, are the main form of transport in greater Buenos Aires, a metropolitan area of around ten million people surrounding the Argentine capital. The route the man covered extended for more than eleven kilometres, according to some local reports.

World.title: Colombia orders deportation of irregular migrants after a decade as the main host country
World.content:
Colombia orders deportation of irregular migrants after a decade as the main host country

24th Monday, August 2026 - 21:37 UTC Full article

“The order to Migration is clear: first those committing crimes, second those who have not regularised their status, who in due course will have to be deported,” he said

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has ordered coordinated operations between the migration authority and the police to begin this week to identify and deport foreigners without regular migration status, marking a shift from the policy the country has maintained for more than a decade as the main destination for Venezuelan migration.

“The order to Migration is clear: first those committing crimes, second those who have not regularised their status, who in due course will have to be deported,” he said during a security council meeting held on Sunday in Barranquilla, the alternate seat of his government. The remarks became known through a leaked video of that meeting. “I will not accept illegal migration. First Colombians, second Colombians and third Colombians,” he added.

Figures on the scope of the measure differ. The Venezuela Observatory at Universidad del Rosario puts the number of Venezuelans without regular status at 848,000, of whom 193,000 would be minors. Migración Colombia data as of January 2026, cited by the outlet La Silla Vacía, indicate that around 82% of Venezuelan migrants hold regular status and close to 500,000 do not. The United Nations refugee agency estimated three million Venezuelans living in Colombia in 2025.

The announcement calls into question the Temporary Protection Statute for Venezuelan Migrants, created by decree in March 2021, which provides a free temporary protection permit and made the country an international reference point on migration regularisation. Colombia took in almost a third of the 7.8 million people who have left Venezuela since 2015, under governments of differing political persuasions.

“A person in irregular status is not a criminal,” said Ronal Rodríguez, a researcher at the observatory, warning against linking irregularity with crime. Congresswoman María Fernanda Carrascal, of the Pacto Histórico, called the measure “an affront to human rights” and said it lacked evidence. Academic Andrés Sampayo estimated the Venezuelan population's contribution to the Colombian economy at around 3 billion dollars a year in consumption, taxes and entrepreneurship.

Implementation faces practical obstacles. Colombia shares a 2,219-kilometre land border with Venezuela, and any mass deportation would require cooperation from the government of acting president Delcy Rodríguez, in a country undergoing a US-backed negotiated transition.

At the same security council meeting, De la Espriella ordered the activation of a rewards system, the strengthening of the informants network and prison transfers to prevent jails from operating as bases for extortion.

World.title: Milei links Lula to the case of the Argentine former adviser detained in Bolivia
World.content:
Milei links Lula to the case of the Argentine former adviser detained in Bolivia

24th Monday, August 2026 - 21:26 UTC Full article

The remarks come during the worst diplomatic crisis between the two countries since the return to democracy

Argentine President Javier Milei has attributed the criminal case against his former adviser Fernando Cerimedo, detained in Bolivia over an attempted femicide, to a regional plot in which he included Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, former Bolivian president Evo Morales and Argentine lawmaker Marcela Pagano. He offered no evidence to support the claim.

“Let's not rule out that behind this is the whole rabble,” he said on Saturday in an interview with Radio Mitre, before listing those names and referring to “castrochavismo,” a term used in the region to describe governments seen as aligned with Cuba and Venezuela. He said it was “a band of castrochavista criminals operating in the region.” In previous days he had accused Lula of running an “anti-Argentine campaign” and of “interfering in electoral processes across the region.”

The remarks come during the worst diplomatic crisis between the two countries since the return to democracy. Brasília recalled its ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations on July 26 and on August 4 downgraded relations to chargé d'affaires level, after Milei took part in a campaign event for Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro at which he referred to Lula in terms the Brazilian government deemed offensive.

In the same interview, Milei distanced himself from Cerimedo. “He is someone who is not part of our movement, who has no link of any kind with us, and with whom we stopped having contact in 2023,” he said. Casa Rosada visitor records examined by the newspaper La Nación show at least thirteen entries by the consultant to the seat of government between December 2023 and June 5, 2024. The logs record who enters and who authorises access, but do not establish meetings with the president. Then interior minister Lisandro Catalán appears as the official who most often approved the visits.

Cerimedo co-founded the digital outlet La Derecha Diario, took part in the communications strategy of Milei's 2023 campaign and advised the campaign of Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz. A judge in Santa Cruz de la Sierra on Friday ordered 180 days of pre-trial detention on a charge of attempted femicide. He denies the accusations and has not been convicted. His business partner in the outlet, Spaniard Javier Negre, told the newspaper Clarín that Cerimedo had agreed to give up his stake before the arrest.

Last week Milei reposted messages on social media questioning the severity of the injuries suffered by Nadia Beller, Cerimedo's former partner. The medical report from the clinic where she was treated records an open, comminuted fracture of the right humerus with metal fragments, requiring emergency surgery.

World.title: Some 25,000 people are seeking housing in Cali two weeks after Colombia's earthquake
World.content:
Some 25,000 people are seeking housing in Cali two weeks after Colombia's earthquake

24th Monday, August 2026 - 21:08 UTC Full article

Among those seeking accommodation, the prevailing perception is of a generalised rise in prices

The municipal survey in Cali, Colombia's third city with more than two million inhabitants, now covers 10,000 families affected by the magnitude 7.4 earthquake of August 10 and estimates around 25,000 people have been left without adequate housing. Many have spent recent days in shelters or with relatives while searching for a rental, in a market strained by the sudden loss of supply.

The city government has carried out detailed assessments of 920 buildings, of which 56 collapsed. Technical analyses place the greatest concentration of damage in commune 19, where close to 200 properties may end up being demolished.

Among those seeking accommodation, the prevailing perception is of a generalised rise in prices. “Rents have gone up in every neighbourhood,” says Laura del Mar Villada, 29, who left her flat in the El Limonar district on the day of the quake and has not yet been able to retrieve her belongings. Manuel Alejandro Molina, 40, who lived with his wife and three-month-old son in the south of the city, says properties that previously cost 2.8 million pesos a month are now being advertised at up to 3.8 million.

Available data, however, point to a localised effect. Economist Sebastián Súlez, a former finance secretary of Jamundí, compiled listings from sixteen portals and estate agencies across 63 neighbourhoods up to August 19 and compared them with a partial snapshot from August 9, the day before the earthquake. Of the eleven comparable neighbourhoods, six recorded falls, one held steady and four rose. In Bellavista, in the affluent western area, the median went from 4.1 to 4.8 million pesos, a rise of 17.1%; in Ciudad Meléndez, in the harder-hit south, prices fell 6.3%. These are asking prices set by landlords, not amounts finally agreed.

Property adviser Harold Andrés Millán observes that owners managing their own properties are asking between 25% and 30% more, while rents on company-managed stock have not changed. Along the corridor where buildings collapsed, he adds, supply and demand have fallen alike.

Mayor Alejandro Eder said days after the earthquake that rents in some areas had doubled and asked the national government for a temporary rent freeze. He also acknowledged a gap in support programmes aimed at middle-income households.

The Colombian Federation of Real Estate Boards clarified that the earthquake does not automatically terminate leases or exempt tenants from payment, though the Civil Code allows termination to be sought if a property becomes uninhabitable. According to the national statistics institute, four in ten Colombian households were renting in 2025, the highest share since at least 2019.

World.title: Unemployment displaces inflation as Argentines' main concern
World.content:
Unemployment displaces inflation as Argentines' main concern

24th Monday, August 2026 - 07:44 UTC Full article

Fear of job loss extends into households: 64% said they were concerned a member of their family could lose their job in the coming months

Unemployment has become the leading problem Argentines want the government to solve, well ahead of inflation, according to the economic expectations report by the polling firm Opina Argentina released over the weekend. Thirty-six percent of respondents placed it first, followed by corruption on 32%, while inflation fell to 11% and insecurity to 9%.

Fear of job loss extends into households: 64% said they were concerned a member of their family could lose their job in the coming months. The survey was conducted online among 1,507 respondents across the country between August 7 and 11. The firm did not publish a margin of error.

Inflation's slide down the list of priorities coincides with a broader deterioration in expectations. Sixty percent of respondents believe their personal situation will worsen in the coming months, seven points more than in July and the highest reading since the end of Alberto Fernández's government. Six in ten of those who voted for Javier Milei and for current senator Patricia Bullrich in the 2023 elections share that outlook.

Household indicators match that perception. Forty-eight percent said they cannot make ends meet and only 18% managed to save over the past month. Sixty-two percent consider it a poor time to buy household appliances and 75% spent nothing on leisure such as cinema, theatre or restaurants. On prices, 55% expect inflation to accelerate and 22% expect it to fall; 63% say the government is not resolving the inflation problem. Fifty-seven percent expect the exchange rate to rise.

The survey also records majority rejection of the three economic bills the executive has sent to Congress: the Inviolability of Private Property Law, the Fiscal Innocence Law and the so-called Super RIGI, a scheme of incentives for large investments in new industries. In all three cases rejection exceeds 58%. The Chamber of Deputies is due to vote on Wednesday on the expansion of Fiscal Innocence, alongside the reform of the central bank's charter.

Other measurements point in the same direction. The Sociopolitical Monitor of the Applied Social Psychology Observatory at the University of Buenos Aires, compiled in July from 2,895 cases, put at 59% those who rate the economic situation as bad or very bad and likewise placed unemployment at the top of concerns.

Monthly inflation in July stood at 2.1%, arrears on credit to individuals reached 17.5% of total lending in June, and the country risk premium passed 470 basis points in August.

World.title: Almost half the minors recruited by armed groups in 2025 were approached via social media
World.content:
Almost half the minors recruited by armed groups in 2025 were approached via social media

24th Monday, August 2026 - 07:32 UTC Full article

The 124-page document, titled “I Thought I Would Never See My Mother Again,” draws on 184 interviews with officials, humanitarian workers, indigenous and community leaders and child protection staff

Some 44% of children and adolescents recruited by armed groups in Colombia during 2025 were approached through social media or platforms such as TikTok and Facebook, according to data from the Special Jurisdiction for Peace cited in a Human Rights Watch report published on Monday.

The 124-page document, titled “I Thought I Would Never See My Mother Again,” draws on 184 interviews with officials, humanitarian workers, indigenous and community leaders and child protection staff. The organisation analysed records held by the Ombudsman's Office and counted at least 1,500 minors recruited since 2021, with a marked rise from 2023: that year the office documented 342 cases, reaching 625 in 2024, an increase of 81%.

“Armed groups in Colombia are recruiting children with impunity, as protection systems fail and social media becomes a more effective recruitment tool,” said Juanita Goebertus, the organisation's Americas director.

The report states that over the past decade around 1% of recruitment complaints led to a criminal investigation and only 0.2% ended in a conviction, mostly of those who carried out the recruitment rather than those bearing greatest responsibility. More than half the cases are concentrated in Cauca department, and FARC dissident groups are behind the majority of complaints.

Between 2020 and 2025 those recruited were most often 15 or 16 years old, though more than 30% of cases involved minors aged between 10 and 14. Child protection officials told the organisation of cases involving children of nine or ten. Human Rights Watch notes that under the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, recruiting children under 15 may constitute a war crime.

Indigenous children account for almost half of documented cases between 2021 and 2025, despite indigenous peoples making up around 4% of Colombia's population. The proportion of girls, averaging 40%, has risen since 2021. Once recruited, minors are usually moved far from their home areas to prevent escape and sever family ties. Boys are assigned to operating drones and to combat; girls are particularly exposed to sexual violence.

The organisation called on Abelardo de la Espriella's government to strengthen prevention policy, ensure adequate funding and reinforce institutional coordination and early warning systems. It also directed recommendations to Congress, the attorney general's office, the Ombudsman's Office, social media operators and the governments of the United States, Canada and European countries.

World.title: Isaac del Toro wins his first Tour of Germany
World.content:
Mexican cyclist Isaac del Toro once again put Mexico at the forefront of international cycling after winning the 40th Deutschland Tour (Tour of Germany), one of the most prestigious stage races on the European calendar.

At 22 years old, this victory makes Del Toro the first Latin American cyclist to win the Tour of Germany, following his recent milestone of becoming the first Mexican cyclist in 36 years to win a stage of the Tour de France.

😱 75 Meter fehlen 🇲🇽 Isaac del Toro zum zweiten Etappensieg! 🇫🇷 Paul Magnier gewinnt in Heilbronn vor 🇳🇱 Danny van Poppel und 🇩🇪 Tim Torn Teutenberg. 👕 Isaac del Toro ist der Gesamtsieger der 🇩🇪 #DeineTour 2026! 🏆#DeutschlandTour pic.twitter.com/8iWFYttYv1 — Tour de France – DE (@letour_de) August 23, 2026

The star cyclist finished the four-stage race with an accumulated time of 17 hours, 39 minutes and 48 seconds, while Frenchman Louis Barré finished second, 53 seconds behind. Swiss rider Marc Hirschi completed the podium, 1:08 back.

Sunday’s final stage covered 156.5 kilometers around Heilbronn, with a route marked by constant climbs and descents.

With the German championship, Del Toro, originally from Ensenada, secured his twentieth professional title since winning his first in 2013 at the Tour de l’Avenir. In 2016, he also won the UAE Tour, Tirreno-Adriatico and Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes.

The Tour of Germany, which ran from Aug. 19 to Aug. 23, also saw the participation of Edgar “Chucky” Cadena, 26, originally from Mexico City.

Chucky was Mexico’s national champion before Del Toro, and is part of a broader generation of athletes working to bring Mexican cyclists back to major competitions.

Participating in Team Storck-MRW Bau, Chucky tried to surprise with an attack 1.5 kilometers from the finish line. With a steady pace in the mountain stages, Chucky’s stamina on the toughest climbs allowed him to quietly climb the standings, securing the No. 10 spot overall.

With reports from Infobae and ESPN

World.title: University of Guadalajara scientists discover 6 ant-killing ‘zombie fungi’
World.content:
Six newly documented species of “zombie fungi” — parasites that hijack the behavior of ants and drive them to their deaths — have been identified in western Jalisco, marking the first scientific record in Mexico of the unusual fungus.

One of the new described species, Ophiocordyceps deltoroi, was named for Guadalajara-born filmmaker Guillermo del Toro, whose work often blends horror and fantasy.

Researchers from the University of Guadalajara (UdeG) found the fungi in a tropical forest near the Haravéri Botanical Garden in San Sebastián del Oeste, Jalisco.

Their study was published online late last year, then drew wider attention this month after reports highlighted the species named for Del Toro.

The six species belong to the Ophiocordyceps unilateralis complex, a group of ant-parasitizing fungi found in tropical forests worldwide.

After infecting an ant by penetrating its outer cuticle, the fungi produce metabolites that alter the ant’s behavior.

The infected ants ultimately clamp their mandibles onto tree bark, leaves or rocks in the forest. After the ant dies, the fungus grows from its body and releases spores, helping infect new hosts.

“It’s both monstrous and beautiful at the same time,” César Ballesteros Aguirre, the UdeG mycologist who led the work, said in a university news release.

The discovery is the first scientific record in Mexico of the so-called “zombie-ant fungi,” according to the university. The team is also studying fungi near metropolitan Guadalajara and parasites of butterflies and wasps.

The fungi are not known to pose a threat to people. Their highly specialized relationships with insect hosts differ sharply from portrayals such as “The Last of Us,” a fictional HBO series in which a mutated Cordyceps fungus spreads to humans and turns them into violent, zombie-like creatures.

Beyond the taxonomy, the UdeG work establishes a baseline for studying Mexico’s fungal biodiversity, the parasites’ relationships with their ant hosts and the chemical compounds they produce.

Their discovery provides a starting point for researchers to catalog the fungi’s metabolites and test them for biological activity.

Some related insect-pathogenic fungi have produced compounds of interest to researchers studying potential biomedical applications and pest control.

However, the new Jalisco species have not been shown to treat any disease, and any potential scientific applications would require substantially more study.

With reports from TV Azteca, Tribuna de México and Infobae

World.title: Mexico’s economy grew 1.4% in Q2 but contracted in June, revised data shows
World.content:
Listen to this article

The Mexican economy grew 1.4% on a quarter-over-quarter basis between April and June and 1.9% in annual terms, according to revised data published by the national statistics agency INEGI on Monday.

Both growth rates were slightly lower than those reported by INEGI in preliminary data published July 30.

However, they still represent a significant improvement from the 0.3% sequential contraction and modest annual growth the Mexican economy registered in the first quarter of 2026. The 1.4% quarter-over-quarter growth between April and June was the best second-quarter result since 2021.

Analysts partially attributed the solid performance in the second quarter to spending related to the FIFA men’s World Cup, which Mexico co-hosted with the United States and Canada in June and July.

INEGI also reported on Monday that the Mexican economy grew 1.2% annually in the first six months of 2026.

Primary sector records strongest Q2 growth

INEGI’s final data shows that Mexico’s primary sector — which includes economic activities related to agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting — expanded 2.4% in the second quarter compared to the first three months of the year. In annual terms, the primary sector grew 4.8%.

The secondary and tertiary sectors also grew in sequential and annual terms in the second quarter, but their expansions were more modest.

The secondary sector — which includes manufacturing, construction and mining as well as electricity, gas and water-related activities — grew 1.6% on a quarter-over-quarter basis and 0.9% annually.

The tertiary, or services, sector grew 1.4% compared to the first quarter of 2026 and 2.3% in annual terms.

INEGI reports a month-over-month contraction in June — and an uptick in inflation

INEGI on Monday also published final economic growth data for June and inflation data for the first half of August.

Mexico’s economy contracted 0.1% in June compared to May and grew 1.7% in annual terms. It was the second consecutive month-over-month decline after a 0.4% contraction in May. The construction sector was a standout performer in June, growing 3% compared to May and 4.2% in annual terms.

INEGI data also showed that Mexico’s annual headline inflation rate rose to 3.26% in the first 15 days of August, up from 3.12% across July.

In the first half of August, Mexico’s annual core inflation rate, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, was 3.93%, down slightly from a 3.95% reading in July.

The outlook for the Mexican economy

Gabriela Siller, director of economic analysis at Banco Base, wrote on X on Monday that her estimate, based on the latest GDP data and the growth of the construction sector in June, was that the Mexican economy will grow 1.4% in 2026.

“Weakness in the consumption of domestic goods and services persists, so it’s still probable that a [sequential] contraction will be recorded in the third quarter,” she wrote.

The Bank of Mexico is forecasting a 1.1% economic expansion this year, while the International Monetary Fund anticipates that the Mexican economy will grow 1.2%. The federal Finance Ministry is more optimistic, forecasting economic growth in the range of 1.8%-2.8% in 2026.

With reports from El Economista

World.title: Another major bust nets weapons, drugs and 20 CJNG-related arrests
World.content:
Federal authorities dismantled a major criminal cell over the weekend, arresting 20 people and seizing weapons and exotic animals.

The joint operation targeted a network allegedly linked to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) and featured simultaneous raids on 36 properties in the states of Hidalgo, Jalisco and Michoacán.

In an official statement, Mexico’s Security Ministry said the Aug. 21-23 operation was the result of intelligence and investigative work by the Defense Ministry, the Navy, the Security Ministry, the Federal Attorney General’s Office and the National Guard.

The statement said that the operation resulted “in the arrest of 20 individuals linked to the CJNG,” adding that “authorities seized 10 firearms (seven handguns and three rifles), drugs, 113 vehicles, tigers, panthers, as well as other animals and birds kept in inadequate conditions.”

Officials also confiscated cash and jewelry, communications equipment, a drone and a drone jammer, while specifying that in addition to the firearms seized, agents gathered up magazines and cartridges of various calibers. The drugs confiscated were said to be unspecified doses of fentanyl and methamphetamine, as well as marijuana.

The Defense Ministry said the 20 detainees were transferred in a Mexican Navy aircraft and placed at the disposal of the Attorney General’s Office (FGR) in Mexico City “to continue with the corresponding investigations and expert analyses to determine their legal status.”

Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said the goal of these operations is not only “to stop those who generate violence, but to steadily weaken the operational, logistical and financial capabilities of criminal organizations.”

García Harfuch said the authorities will “continue with coordinated intelligence, investigation and territorial presence efforts” to protect and defend the public interest.

The outcome of this latest tactical operation brings to 32 the total number of alleged CJNG members apprehended by security forces in less than a week.

On Aug. 19, the Army led a major security operation in Michoacán targeting CJNG leader Heraclio Guerrero Martínez, alias “El Tío Lako.” The 15-hour raid resulted in nine to 12 arrests — including the target’s partner and daughter.

With reports from Excelsior, Milenio and Aristegui Noticias

World.title: Why Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya returned to office for only 48 hours
World.content:
Rubén Rocha Moya, the Sinaloa governor who is accused of drug trafficking by U.S. prosecutors, returned to office on Friday — only to ask to go on leave again the very next day.

The 77-year-old governor’s submission of a request to take indefinite leave came after representatives of his own party — Morena — rejected his decision to return to the governorship of Sinaloa almost four months after he first left office. The Sinaloa Congress approved his leave request on Sunday.

In a social media post on Saturday, President Claudia Sheinbaum also indicated that she didn’t agree with Rocha’s decision to return to office. The president — the leader of the “fourth transformation” (4T) movement with which Rocha is also affiliated — explicitly expressed that position on Monday.

Rocha, who became governor of Sinaloa in late 2021, first decided to take leave in early May shortly after the unsealing of a U.S. indictment accusing him and nine other current and former Sinaloa-based officials of drug trafficking in league with the Sinaloa Cartel.

The U.S. Justice Department said on April 29 that the governor allegedly attended meetings with “the Chapitos” — sons of convicted drug trafficker Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán — and allowed the Sinaloa Cartel faction they lead to “operate with impunity in Sinaloa.”

Rocha, who is also accused of weapons offenses, promptly rejected the accusations against him. To date, he has avoided extradition to the United States as — according to the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) in Mexico — U.S. authorities have not presented sufficient evidence against him. Sheinbaum has endorsed the FGR’s view and stressed that Mexican legal processes and sovereignty must be respected. However, now, more than ever, she is seeking to distance herself and her government from Rocha, whose indictment has raised serious and broader questions about alleged corruption and alleged collusion between Morena and organized crime.

The governor’s decision to return to office on Friday surprised — and in some cases outraged — millions of Mexicans, including members of the federal government. His brief return to office restored his constitutional immunity from prosecution, according to experts, but he presumably lost that immunity (called fuero in Mexico) by going on leave once again.

Here is a timeline of relevant events between Friday. Aug. 21 and Monday, Aug. 24.

Friday morning: Rocha announces his return to office

In a social media post shortly before 10 a.m. on Friday, Rocha announced that he had resumed his position as governor of Sinaloa.

“It is my duty to fulfill the mandate of the people of Sinaloa, who elected me as head of the executive branch to govern until October 31, 2027,” he wrote.

“During the period of my temporary leave from office, which I requested from the State Congress on May 1 of this year, I placed myself at the disposal of our country’s justice system in order to be investigated regarding the false accusations … that a U.S. government office leveled against me without any evidence, seeking to undermine our national sovereignty through its statements and slander,” Rocha wrote.

The governor wrote that he had personally appeared before the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) during his leave of absence. That institute, he said, determined that there was no evidence against him.

“In other words, I haven’t committed any crime,” Rocha wrote.

“… Today I return to fulfilling my duties as Governor of Sinaloa with a clear conscience, with my head held high, and with the power of the truth on our side.”

Early Friday afternoon: SEGOB says that Rocha’s decision to return to office was a ‘personal’ one

In a statement issued early Friday afternoon, the federal Interior Ministry (SEGOB) sought to distance the federal government from Rocha’s decision to return to office.

“The Interior Ministry reports that the decision of Dr. Rubén Rocha Moya to resume his duties as governor of the state of Sinaloa is exclusively a determination of a personal nature,” SEGOB said.

The ministry noted that the FGR opened investigations into the 10 people accused of drug trafficking and weapons offenses by U.S. prosecutors, among whom is Rocha, a Morena senator and the mayor of Culiacán.

SEGOB highlighted that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has asked the U.S. Department of Justice on repeated occasions to “provide the evidence that supports the accusations.”

“In that sense, it is up to the Federal Attorney General’s Office, within the domain of its powers and in accordance with the advance of the investigations, to provide additional information it considers pertinent,” the Interior Ministry said.

Late Friday afternoon: Morena lawmakers speak out

Later on Friday afternoon, Morena deputies expressed their opposition to Rocha’s decision to return to office.

In a statement, Morena deputies called on the governor to “reconsider his decision” so that the FGR and “other authorities” can continue and conclude their investigations “with full autonomy.”

Comunicado del Grupo Parlamentario de Morena pic.twitter.com/5S3wYRYkB7 — Arturo Ávila. (@arturoavila_mx) August 22, 2026

Morena senators echoed SEGOB’s sentiment, saying in a statement that Rocha’s decision to return to office was a “personal and individual action.”

Friday evening: Morena governors weigh in

The Morena governors of 22 states as well as Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada and the Green Party governor of San Luis Potosí released a statement on Friday evening expressing their opposition to Rocha’s return to office in Sinaloa.

“In the fourth transformation, individual decisions will never be above the collective project or the citizens’ mandate,” said the 4T political leaders.

“… No authority is empowered to act at the margin of the law or to take unilateral decisions that threaten constitutional order or republican dialogue,” they said.

“Personal or group political projects have no place when they counteract the well-being of the nation. We call on Dr. Rubén Rocha Moya to act with maturity and responsibility,” said the 23 governors and Brugada.

“Politics is an exercise of congruence. Excess and factional decisions go against principles of honesty and loyalty that we swore to uphold.”

Saturday morning: Sheinbaum enters the fray

In a social media post on Friday morning, Sheinbaum announced that she was sick with the flu and therefore didn’t perform any public duties that day, and didn’t comment on Rocha’s return to office.

The president returned to social media on Saturday morning to publish a message that was clearly aimed at Rocha, although she didn’t mention the governor by name.

“No personal interest can ever be above the interests of the people and the nation,” she wrote.

“And certainly not when what is being placed above Mexico is not the well-being of its people, but the naked ambition of power for power’s sake,” Sheinbaum said.

“… Power without principles becomes arrogance; power without limits becomes abuse; and power that forgets the people ultimately finds itself at odds with history,” she wrote.

Ningún interés personal puede estar jamás por encima de los intereses del pueblo y de la Nación. Y mucho menos cuando aquello que se pretende colocar por encima de México no es el bienestar de su gente, sino la ambición desnuda del poder por el poder.

Porque el poder sin… — Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) August 22, 2026

“Mexico deserves public servants who understand that positions are temporary, but the responsibility to the nation is eternal. The people are not here to feed personal ambitions: they are here to demand that their dignity, their future, and their hope be defended. Above any name, any group, and any personal interest stand the people and the nation.”

In a separate social media post on Saturday morning, the director of the Sinaloa-based Noroeste newspaper, Adrían López Ortiz, wrote:

“I see many outsiders saying that Sinaloenses are speaking out against Rocha. I’ll give you a fact. Yesterday, @noroestemx tried to ask people in the center of Culiacán what they thought about his return [but] they were scared to respond on camera.”

Sinaloa is a violence-plagued state where the Los Chapitos and Los Mayos factions of the Sinaloa Cartel are engaged in a long-running and extremely bloody civil war. Cartel violence has ravaged the Sinaloa economy and led many residents to take extra safety precautions, such as limiting their movements at night.

Saturday evening: Rocha heeds Sheinbaum’s words

In a social media post on Saturday evening, Rocha published a letter addressed to the president of the Sinaloa Congress in which he requested “temporary leave” of an “indefinite nature” from his job as governor.

Above the letter, he wrote: “Sinaloa, the nation and the transformation movement are above everything.”

Sunday morning: Sinaloa Congress approves Rocha’s leave request

In an extraordinary session on Sunday morning, Sinaloa state lawmakers unanimously approved Rocha’s request to go on indefinite leave.

Monday morning: Sheinbaum says Rocha’s decision to return to office was ‘imprudent’

At her Monday morning press conference, Sheinbaum said that she found out about Rocha’s decision to return to the governorship of Sinaloa via his social media post on Friday.

“I didn’t have any prior knowledge that he wanted to return to his duties in the state of Sinaloa,” she said.

“The truth is that I didn’t think it was appropriate, to say the least,” Sheinbaum said.

Later in the press conference, the president explicitly said she didn’t agree with Rocha’s decision to return to the governorship of Sinaloa.

“At the very least, I thought it was imprudent,” Sheinbaum said.

“… Nothing personal can be above the interests of the people of Sinaloa and the people of Mexico,” she said.

Sheinbaum said on Sunday that Rocha’s decision to once again leave the governorship was “the best thing for Sinaloa.”

On Monday, she noted that the Sinaloa Congress has to appoint an interim governor until a new governor takes office in late 2027 following the Sinaloa gubernatorial election in June of next year. She said that the interim governor should be a person who is honest, professional and dedicated to “the people of Sinaloa.”

Sheinbaum subsequently described claims that former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador told Rocha to return to the governorship of Sinaloa as “political fiction.”

World.title: MND Local: Flight cuts and water relief in Guadalajara, and Jalisco’s tequila economy
World.content:
This week brings another round of international flight schedule changes at Guadalajara International Airport. Also in this week’s update, the government clarifies who is eligible for 80% discounts from SIAPA due to poor-quality tap water, plus an update on Jalisco’s tequila economy.

Aeroméxico suspends flights from Guadalajara to Northern California, Chicago

Last week, Aeroméxico suspended several important routes between Guadalajara and the U.S., including nonstop flights to San Francisco, Sacramento, Fresno and Chicago, according to schedule filings tracked by AeroRoutes.

The route suspensions are in effect from now until mid-December, with no clarity on whether they might resume after that.

Aeroméxico’s suspended routes and dates in effect

Route Dates of suspension Guadalajara to Chicago (ORD) Aug. 17, 2026 – Dec. 16, 2026 Guadalajara to San Francisco (SFO) Aug. 17, 2026 – Dec. 16, 2026 Guadalajara to Fresno (FAT) Aug. 17, 2026 – Dec. 16, 2026 Guadalajara to Sacramento (SMF) Aug. 17, 2026 – Dec. 16, 2026

Under Aeroméxico’s disruption rules, ticketed customers on canceled routes are entitled to a route and schedule change or a refund. Before calling the airline to request rebooking, it is a good idea to confirm that your itinerary is no longer available on its website.

It is also wise to keep any receipts for hotels, ground transport and nonrefundable side bookings tied to your original Aeroméxico itinerary. Those costs can influence whether the airline grants a reissue, refund or full cancellation of the original ticket.

Competing carriers such as United Airlines and the ultra-low-cost carriers Volaris and Viva Aerobus still service these cities to and from Guadalajara, so travelers have a few alternatives left that eliminate the need to connect in Mexico City.

Who is eligible for 80% discounts from SIAPA due to poor water quality?

A hot topic in Guadalajara lately has been the question of who is — and is not — eligible for a discount on their water bill from SIAPA (the Intermunicipal Water and Sewerage Services System in Jalisco) stemming from chronic water quality issues in the Guadalajara metropolitan area.

After weeks of speculation, we finally have some answers.

As of Aug. 17, an 80% discount will be applied to water bills in 203 neighborhoods in Guadalajara, Zapopan, Tlaquepaque and Tonalá affected by serious water quality problems. The initiative aims to compensate users who have reported various problems with water coming from their taps, including foul-smelling, dirty or discolored water.

The Jalisco Congress formalized the benefit, and the SIAPA Governing Board approved the first list of beneficiary neighborhoods, with details published on Aug. 14 in the Official Gazette of Jalisco.

Popular expatriate neighborhoods such as Ladrón de Guevara, Santa Teresita and Providencia in Guadalajara, as well as Chapalita and Seattle in Zapopan, are all eligible for the discount. To see the full list of neighborhoods, check Annex A of this document.

How to claim the SIAPA discount

Economic relief is aimed at residential users and small businesses in the designated neighborhoods who consume up to 25 cubic meters of water per month. Those who consume more than this amount are ineligible.

To qualify, households and businesses must also demonstrate that they are up to date on all of their payments to SIAPA to receive the discount. In other words, those who stopped paying for contaminated water out of frustration and are still in arrears cannot obtain a discount.

There are also 32 neighborhoods still under review for eligibility, so if your neighborhood is not on the current list, it may still be added later as SIAPA makes adjustments.

Residents can access the discount until Dec. 15, 2026.

Tequila exports showed signs of recovery in the first half of 2026

Despite the trade uncertainty surrounding negotiations of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), the tequila business appears to be resurgent in 2026, following sluggish results in 2025.

According to figures from the Tequila Regulatory Council (CRT), total tequila exports during the first half of this year reached 215 million liters, up 3.4% from the 208 million liters exported abroad in the same period of 2025. The U.S. remains the largest export market for Mexican tequila by far (taking roughly 81% of the total).

Following a period of explosive growth in demand from 2020 to 2024 where growth averaged 8.5% per year, demand for Jalisco’s most famous beverage has leveled off. The slowdown stems mainly from reduced demand for super-premium tequila in the U.S., as consumers traded down or explored sobriety following the coronavirus pandemic’s well-documented drinking binge.

In response, Jalisco’s producers have been working to correct an agave oversupply problem (too many fields were planted during boom times) and develop new business in Europe, Latin America and Asia to reduce their dependence on the U.S. consumer.

Based on the trend year to date, the Tequila Regulatory Council is cautiously optimistic for better times ahead for the state’s 229 authorized producers and more than 3,400 registered brands.

MND Writer Dawn Stoner is reporting from Guadalajara.

World.title: Profepa clears 6 dolphins for relocation from shuttered Cancún dolphinarium
World.content:
Six of the nine dolphins living at the now-shuttered Dolphin Discovery installations, located within the former Ventura Park in Cancún, Quintana Roo, are considered candidates to begin a preparation process for a possible relocation, according to a report by the Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection (Profepa).

The move comes amid concerns about the health and safety of the animals, which remain under the care of Mexico’s environmental authority following the closure of the dolphinarium in October last year after videos surfaced of the dolphins displaying extreme distress.

Profepa stated that the nine dolphins – two females and seven males – are in delicate clinical condition, meaning their transfer cannot be immediate and each animal will require an individual protocol.

Since May, Profepa has been working to medically stabilize the dolphins through veterinary checkups, laboratory tests and monitoring of their behavior, feeding and response to treatment, the agency told Mongabay.

However, activist groups in defense of animal rights, including Veeleaf and Tide Breakers, have shared images and videos criticizing the care of the nine dolphins that remain in captivity. Reportedly, the dolphins are in small pools where they can barely move, are fed smaller portions of food than required and spend all their time in the sun, with no shade.

The future of these dolphins is tied to a reform that sought to transform the operations of dolphinariums in Mexico.

In July 2025, the Mexican Senate unanimously approved a nationwide ban on dolphin and other marine mammal shows, as well as the breeding of marine mammals in captivity except for conservation purposes.

The new regulations mandate the transfer of cetaceans to marine pens, or fenced-off ocean enclosures that slowly reintroduce the dolphins to their natural habitat, and limit interactions with those already under human care, prohibiting practices that could compromise their well-being.

However, the regulations needed to establish the application criteria have not been published yet; hence, the nine dolphins remain in the same pools where they have spent a good part of their lives.

The organization Empty the Tanks is demanding that the dolphins be temporarily transferred to existing marine pools at the Dolphin Discovery facilities in Isla Mujeres and Chankanaab, Cozumel. “We are not asking that they be released into the ocean. We are asking for a responsible, feasible measure backed by scientific evidence: that they be allowed to live in a much more natural environment while receiving the care they need,” the organization said in a statement.

According to a statement by Profepa, “All the decisions that have been made aim to ensure the best possible well-being of the dolphins, to help them survive in the best way possible and to alleviate their suffering.”

“We know that moving them to a semi-open enclosure at sea would be an improvement, but first we must guarantee that this move does not cost them their lives,” the statement continues.

With reports from Infobae, Por Esto! and Reportur

World.title: Aura farming battles make their debut in Mexico
World.content:
With a nod to the “You got served” hip-hop dance battle craze of two decades ago, kids and young adults in Mexico have begun to stage “aura farming” battles in public squares across the country.

What the heck is aura farming, you ask? Fair question …

Aura farming is a viral internet slang trend that describes doing intentional, effortless things to look confident or charismatic. Gen Alpha and Gen Z use the term to describe doing something to improve your “vibe,” your style or your perceived social status, without seeming like you’re trying too hard.

It even warrants a definition in Merriam-Webster: “the act of doing something to look cool, impressive, stylish, etc., especially — and importantly — without trying too hard.”

The concept grew on TikTok and Instagram, combining the video game concept of “farming” (carrying out repetitive actions for points), before dancing was attached to it, eventually evolving into physical “aura battles” in parks and streets across Latin America.

In Mexico City, three notorious aura farming battles took place last week: on Friday at the esplanade of the Palace of Fine Arts in Mexico City; on Saturday at the Monument to the Revolution; and on Sunday in the Condesa neighborhood (where there was even a prize of 3,000 pesos, or US $177).

The craze has reached beyond the capital, too.

Aura battles have recently been staged in Juárez Park in Xalapa, the capital of Veracruz, and children as young as six years old participated in a competition in Torreón, Coahuila.

Compiten en Concurso para "Farmear Aura" en Veracruz

Watch this video on YouTube

The “battles” attract massive crowds who watch participants compete symbolically with poses, dances, gestures and meme references to demonstrate who has more “aura.”

A winner is determined by crowd reaction (the volume of cheers, applause, laughter) and by the general impact made during the face-off. Essentially, the social presence displayed is “scored” like an imaginary video game.

Unfortunately, the events also have their detractors. The municipal council of Ignacio de la Llave, Veracruz, officially prohibited aura battles in public parks, arguing that it was not due to the theme or content of the competition, but rather “a strict matter of administrative procedures and regulations for public spaces.”

CNN traces the origin of aura farming to 2024 and said it gained international attention last year through viral videos of 11-year-old Indonesian Rayyan Arkan Dikha dancing at the front of a boat in a traditional rowing competition. Social media users commented on the high levels of “aura” the boy possessed and it took off from there.

The trend has become particularly popular in Latin America: A “championship” was staged at the University of Costa Rica in San Juan on Aug. 18 and several tournaments were organized in São Paulo, Brazil, this summer.

With reports from CNN, LatinUS, Infobae and Telediario

The Treasury Steadies The Market For Its Own Paper

Cash instead of issuance

Long American borrowing costs eased on Tuesday after reports that the Treasury could use its cash balance to fund larger repurchases of its own bonds. Doing so would reduce how much short-dated paper it needs to issue.

Thirty-year borrowing steadied at about 5.2297%, down from 5.2497% on Monday. Ten-year borrowing was flat near 4.7021% and two-year near 4.2421%.

Why the second attempt matters

A repurchase programme means the government buying back its own outstanding bonds to support demand at the long end. Funding it from cash rather than new issuance avoids adding to the supply that caused the problem.

A similar announcement earlier this month held for roughly a day before fading. That this one had to follow so soon is the part worth noting.

Three Tests In Three Days

Confidence, inflation, a speech

Consumer confidence is published this morning, the inflation measure the central bank prefers follows on Wednesday, and Chair Warsh speaks in Wyoming on Friday.

Each answers a different part of the same question. Confidence tells you whether households have noticed; inflation tells you whether elevated oil has reached the figures the committee weighs; the speech tells you whether the institution intends to lead the market or follow it.

Markets Are Pricing Tightening Into A Slowing Economy

One quarter-point by year end

Traders currently expect one increase of a quarter point before the end of the year. That is tightening priced into an economy most people still describe as slowing.

The three members who dissented in July for an increase look less isolated with each week that long borrowing costs stay elevated.

A borrower that has to keep intervening in the market for its own paper is telling you something about that market.

One Company’s Accounts Still Move Three Continents

Ninety-two billion dollars

Canada Supplies The Day’s Only Hard Figure

Canadian wholesale sales for July are expected to have fallen 1.3% on the month, against a rise of 2.8% previously. It is the first monthly read covering the period in which the tariff threat became a certainty.

The duties are in their fourth day and Ottawa’s matching measures remain set for 8 September. Neither government has announced further talks.

What This Means From Latin America

The reading is unchanged in direction and slightly better in degree. Long dollar borrowing eased a little, and it eased because the borrower stepped in rather than because lenders relaxed.

The second point is about what is being priced. A market expecting a rate increase into a slowing economy is a market that has stopped believing inflation will fall on its own.

For regional borrowers the practical test arrives Wednesday and Friday. The July inflation figure and the Wyoming address will set the price of dollar funding for the rest of the quarter.

The Bigger Picture The distinction between debt management and monetary policy matters here. The central bank sets the price of money; the Treasury is now managing the market for its own paper alongside it. Our 24 August dossier noted that the previous intervention had stopped working. A second one followed within a day, which is consistent with that reading. Canadian wholesale sales are the first hard evidence of what the trade dispute has cost, covering the month in which the threat hardened into certainty.

German Confidence Jumped, And By A Lot

A substantial beat

The ifo business climate index for Germany rose to 88.8 in August from 86.7 in July. Economists had expected 87.2, so this is a substantial beat rather than a rounding difference.

Both halves moved. The assessment of current conditions climbed to 88.5 from 86.5, and expectations for the next six months reached 89.1 from 86.8.

And the reported reason is unusual

The institute reported that companies were more satisfied with current conditions, significantly upgraded their outlook, and described declining uncertainty. That last item came despite another increase in energy prices.

Firms saying they feel less uncertain in a month when their input costs rose again is not the ordinary pattern.

The Line That Complicates It

Production expectations without orders

Manufacturing recorded the strongest rebound of any sector, with its balance improving to minus 4.2 from minus 9.6, and firms expecting production to increase over the coming three months.

In the same breath the institute recorded that order books remained weak. German manufacturers expect to produce more without yet having the orders to produce it against.

Why It Might Still Be Right

What a sentiment survey is for

Confidence surveys often turn before the hard data, which is the entire reason anybody reads them. Companies see enquiry volumes and tender pipelines months before any of it becomes a recorded order.

A broad-based improvement across manufacturing, services, trade and construction is harder to dismiss than a single sector’s optimism.

German manufacturers expect to produce more without yet having the orders to produce it against. That is a forecast about demand rather than a report of it.

Against A Very Different Backdrop

Confidence up, borrowing costs up

This lands three days after German thirty-year borrowing reached its costliest since 2011 and the finance ministry attributed record issuance to defence spending. Berlin sold two-year paper this morning against a previous level of 2.78%.

Firms are more confident and their government is paying more to borrow, in the same week. Both can be true and they pull in opposite directions.

France Remains The Continent’s Exposed Position

Deficit, budget, election

Borrowing remains near levels last seen in 2008, with the deficit expected to stay above five per cent and budget measures unagreed. A presidential election follows next year.

The European Central Bank Governing Council meets on 9 and 10 September in Berlin.

What This Means From Latin America

The caution is about sequencing. European buyers who feel better will not place orders until they have customers of their own, and a confidence reading is not a purchase order.

This brief reported on 21 August that German factory strength rested on defence procurement and precautionary stockpiling. Neither generates the follow-on orders a genuine recovery needs.

For exporters of industrial inputs the honest position is that this reading is real information about mood and not yet information about output. Whether the second follows the first is what the autumn will settle.

The Bigger Picture The most encouraging detail is that uncertainty fell in a month when energy prices rose again. Firms appear to have absorbed the energy question rather than merely stopped noticing it. The improvement was broad-based rather than concentrated, which is what separates a credible sentiment reading from a single-sector story. Sentiment surveys reverse faster than they rise. If orders fail to arrive through the autumn, this reading will retreat toward the activity data rather than pull it upward.

Two Companies, One Question, Opposite Answers

Raise or return

Alibaba launched a share sale of 10.2 billion dollars on Tuesday, priced at a steep discount, to fund its artificial intelligence ambitions. It comes a day after Samsung Electronics said it would return as much as 110 trillion won to investors.

One decided the money earns more with shareholders and the other decided it earns more in data centres. A market that punishes both is not judging capital allocation — it is admitting it cannot yet tell whether the underlying investment earns anything.

The Discount Is The Message

What selling below market price means

A company sells shares below the going price when it wants the money quickly and is not confident of getting it otherwise. The discount is the cost of certainty.

For a company of Alibaba’s size, ten billion dollars is not transformative. The willingness to pay a discount says the capacity it buys is wanted urgently.

Then The Day Turned

Opened down, closed up

Tokyo opened down and closed up. The Nikkei finished 0.5% higher at 65,856.43 after trading below 65,000 during the session, and Seoul closed 0.68% higher at 6,742.74 having been down more than two per cent.

Chip suppliers led the reversal, with SK Hynix higher and Samsung little changed. Readers who saw only the morning reports will have a different picture of Tuesday than the closes support.

Only one of them can be reading the returns on this build-out correctly. That is why both were marked down, because the market cannot yet tell which.

Everything Is Waiting On One Company

Accounts nobody in Asia will publish

The reversal did not come from anything that happened in Asia. It came from expectations about an American chip maker reporting later this week, whose quarterly revenue analysts put near ninety-two billion dollars.

Seoul, Tokyo, Shanghai and Hong Kong spent Tuesday trading a set of accounts none of them will publish.

And Beijing Is Committing Money Elsewhere

Indonesia

Chinese investment into Indonesia reached 3.9 billion dollars in the first half of this year, and the two governments agreed last week to deepen cooperation on minerals, energy and technology.

Chinese firms there have complained of heavy regulation and a new nickel pricing formula raising their costs. China is committing capital abroad while its largest technology company asks the market for more at home.

What This Means From Latin America

The exposure is indirect but real. If the spending is justified, demand for the metals and energy this build-out consumes holds; if it is not, the correction reaches every supplier of those inputs.

The second lesson is procedural. Tokyo and Seoul opened sharply lower and closed higher, and anyone reading only the morning wires has the day backwards.

The third is about concentration. When one American company’s quarterly accounts determine how four Asian markets trade, the region has outsourced its own price discovery — and so has anyone hedging against it.

The Bigger Picture Set against Samsung, the contrast is exact. One company concluded there was nothing better to do with eighty billion dollars than return it; the other concluded ten billion of new money was worth a discount to obtain. There is a version where both are right. Alibaba needs capacity for its own platforms while Samsung sells components into a market it expects to soften. The Bank of Korea decides on Thursday, immediately after two days of unusually loud corporate signalling about the region’s investment appetite.

An Offer Of Mediation Meets A Refusal To Mediate

Washington offers, Addis Ababa declines

Massad Boulos, the American president’s senior adviser on African affairs, said Washington is ready to resume mediation between Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, offering to facilitate talks and provide technical support.

Ethiopia’s water and energy minister, Habtamu Itefa, answered that his country does not need permission from anybody to develop its water resources. He rejected calls for joint management of the dam.

And he went further than the dam

Habtamu said Ethiopia built the dam without seeking permission and would do the same if it decided to develop other river basins. Addis Ababa is planning additional hydropower projects on the Blue Nile.

That is a sovereignty argument rather than a water argument, and it is the more difficult of the two to mediate.

What Each Side Is Actually Protecting

A rulebook against a running asset

Egypt draws the large majority of its fresh water from the Nile and wants a legally binding agreement covering how the dam is filled and operated, particularly through droughts.

Ethiopia has an inaugurated dam with an official capacity of five thousand megawatts and a country short of electricity. Having built the asset, it has no obvious reason to accept constraints on running it.

Sudan Sits In Between, As Usual

Why three-way agreement never forms

Khartoum has at times differed from Cairo, noting that regulated flows and imported electricity could benefit it. It has also raised concerns about the dam’s safety and about how releases are coordinated.

Sudan is not simply a smaller Egypt, and treating it as one has defeated a decade of negotiators.

You can split a river; you cannot split a principle.

The Arrangement Currently Holding Is The Weather

A drought is what the rulebook is for

For most of the period since the reservoir began filling, rainfall has been consistent and downstream flows have not been materially affected. The absence of an agreement has cost nobody anything.

A drought is the situation a rulebook exists for, and it is precisely the situation in which no party will want to be bound by one they did not sign.

Elsewhere On The Continent

Accra, Kampala, Monrovia, Pretoria

Ghana’s cedi came under renewed pressure near 11.00 to the dollar against 10.90 a week earlier, with auction bids of 399 million dollars against 125 million allocated. Uganda’s central bank held its rate at 9.75%.

Liberia’s former vice president has been arrested, triggering a political confrontation, and a South African citizenship case involving a Nigerian-born woman was postponed to 2027.

What This Means From Latin America

The Nile dispute has an exact counterpart in this hemisphere. Itaipu, on the Paraná, is jointly owned and jointly operated by Brazil and Paraguay under a treaty signed before a single turbine was installed.

That is the difference. The rulebook came before the dam in South America, and in East Africa the dam came first and the rulebook has still not arrived.

The contrast is instructive rather than flattering to anybody. Itaipu has generated its own decades of argument over pricing and debt, but it has never generated an argument about whether an agreement exists.

The Bigger Picture Neither position is a bluff and neither side has an obvious concession available, which is why a decade of mediation has produced nothing. Washington hosted talks during the president’s first term that produced no agreement, and he wrote to Cairo in January offering to restart mediation. Egypt and Sudan welcomed that offer and Ethiopia said little. This week Ethiopia stopped saying little. That is the development, and it makes the American offer harder to accept than it was in January.

Africa Intelligence Brief August 25, 2026: What We Are Watching

Ethiopia’s next projects — Each new dam makes agreement on the first one harder.
